entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from or have transited a country with risk of transmission, and it is routinely demanded as part of a Bolivian visa application. entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from or have transited a country with risk of transmission. Bolivia's Migration Directorate also lists a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate among the requirements for a tourist visa or stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. Vaccination is strongly recommended — and sometimes checked on domestic flights — before traveling to the lowland departments of Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando, Tarija or the Yungas.
entries.note: DIGEMIG's requirement reads 'Certificado de vacuna contra la fiebre amarilla vigente, si visitará zonas endémicas de alto riesgo' — conditional on visiting high-risk areas, not a routine part of every visa application.

entries.old: appliesTo all: Airlines check for a confirmed onward or return ticket, and it is part of the documentation for a visa application. Overland arrivals are asked less consistently.
entries.new: appliesTo visa-applicants: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must show a travel itinerary or return ticket, an invitation from a person legally resident in Bolivia registered with the Migration Directorate, or a hotel booking. Airlines may also check for an onward ticket at check-in.
entries.note: DIGEMIG lists the itinerary/return ticket as one of three alternatives (with a registered invitation letter or a hotel booking) among tourist-visa requirements; no official page imposes it on visa-free arrivals.

entries.old: required false: No fixed sum is published for visa-free visitors, but visa applicants must show economic solvency — typically recent bank statements. Officers may ask arriving tourists to demonstrate funds for the stay.
entries.new: required true (visa applicants): Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must prove economic solvency with a sworn declaration backed by documents, such as recent bank statements. No minimum sum is published, and none is set for visa-free visitors.
entries.note: DIGEMIG lists 'Solvencia económica acreditada mediante declaración jurada respaldada documentalmente' among tourist-visa requirements.

entries.old: A customs declaration is completed on arrival at international airports and land borders, covering goods, cash and agricultural products.
entries.new: Before entering or leaving Bolivia, travelers fill in customs Form 250, a sworn declaration of new goods carried in accompanied baggage (on entry) and of currency (on entry and exit). It is available pre-printed or electronically.
entries.note: Aduana Nacional: 'Previo a su ingreso o salida de territorio boliviano, LLENE el Form. 250 de mercancías nuevas (ingreso) y divisas (ingreso y salida).'

Larger sums must be moved through a financial institution regulated by ASFI. Customs withholds 30% of undeclared currency, and of any amount above the limits.

entries.new: Group 2 nationalities can, at La Paz (El Alto), Santa Cruz (Viru Viru) and the main land borders. Bring a passport valid for at least six months, a recent 4x4 cm photo on a white background, a travel itinerary or return ticket (or a registered invitation letter or hotel booking), documents backing a sworn statement of your funds, a yellow fever certificate if you will visit high-risk areas, and the fee of 300 UFV, paid at Banco Unión once the officer authorizes it. Processing takes up to 10 minutes at the border. Applying at a consulate first is slower but avoids surprises at a remote border post.

Second-group nationalities need 90 days' validity, and nationalities that need a visa need 180 days. Airlines may apply stricter checks of their own.

entries.old: Violent crime against tourists is uncommon by regional standards, but the political situation since 2018 has made Nicaragua unpredictable: protests are banned, police may stop and question foreigners, and travelers have been denied entry or expelled over social-media posts or NGO links. Several governments advise reconsidering non-essential travel.
entries.new: Political activity is the main risk for visitors: it is illegal for foreigners to take part in any political activity, and joining a protest, attending political meetings or campaigns, or using the national blue-and-white colours in a campaign can lead to arrest, detention or deportation. Violent crime does affect foreign nationals, including attacks on people in vehicles and 'express kidnapping' in unauthorised taxis, so use radio-dispatched or red-plate authorised taxis and avoid markets and bus stations on foot after dark.
entries.note: The FCDO page no longer supports two claims in the old text: it says foreign nationals have been affected by violent crime (not that it is uncommon), and neither the FCDO nor Canada (which says 'exercise a high degree of caution') advises reconsidering travel. Level unchanged.

Belarus currently waives visas for citizens of roughly 40 European countries — the whole EU and the UK included — for stays of up to 30 days under a temporary decree, and CIS citizens enter freely under bilateral agreements; a separate 30-day waiver covers many more nationalities arriving by air at Minsk National Airport. Everyone else needs an embassy visa, and land-border rules are restrictive and change often.
entries.new: Belarus waives visas for citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland among them — for stays of up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia) at any international road or rail crossing, under a regime that runs until December 31, 2026; CIS citizens enter freely under bilateral agreements, and a separate 30-day waiver covers many more nationalities arriving by air at Minsk National Airport. Everyone else needs an embassy visa.
entries.note: The MFA page names 38 European states, 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania, Latvia), entry at all international road and rail crossings, valid until 31 Dec 2026. "Roughly 40" and "land-border rules are restrictive" replaced with the official statement.

entries.old: It depends on your passport. Citizens of roughly 40 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland and the Balkans — currently enter visa-free for up to 30 days under a temporary decree, and CIS citizens are visa-free under bilateral agreements. Many other nationalities (US, Canada, Japan and more) get 30 days visa-free only when flying in and out of Minsk National Airport. Everyone else needs a visa from a Belarusian embassy.
entries.new: It depends on your passport. Citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and the European microstates — enter visa-free for up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, and no more than 90 days in a calendar year) at any international road or rail crossing until December 31, 2026, and CIS citizens are visa-free under bilateral agreements. Many other nationalities (US, Canada, Japan and more) get 30 days visa-free only when flying in and out of Minsk National Airport. Everyone else needs a visa from a Belarusian embassy.
entries.note: "Roughly 40 ... and the Balkans" replaced with the MFA list of 38 states (Serbia, Montenegro and Albania are visa-free under separate arrangements, not this regime).

entries.old: Venezuela is one of the most dangerous countries in the hemisphere for visitors. Violent crime, armed robbery and express kidnapping are common in Caracas and other cities; there is a real risk of wrongful detention of foreign nationals; power cuts, fuel and medicine shortages are routine; and the Colombian border states are affected by armed groups. The United States and several other governments advise against all travel, and consular help for travelers in trouble is extremely limited.
entries.new: UK: against all travel to the border areas, Zulia, the Orinoco Mining Arc and Delta Amacuro south of the Orinoco, all but essential elsewhere; US: Level 3 reconsider travel, Level 4 for the Colombian border region, Amazonas, Apure, Táchira, Guárico, Aragua outside Maracay and rural Bolívar
entries.note: The text said the United States advises against all travel. The US advisory is now 'Venezuela - Level 3: Reconsider Travel' ('The travel advisory level decreased to 3. The "Wrongful Detention," "Unrest," and "Other" risk indicators were removed'), read from Wayback 20260513160915 because travel.state.gov answers 403 (Cloudflare) and has no later 200 capture. It also says a phased resumption of US embassy operations began in January 2026 and routine consular services remain suspended. The FCDO pages (live, updated 2 September 2026) give the area warnings, the detention of foreigners accused of terrorism, airport questioning, shortages and the La Guaira disaster zone after the 24 June earthquakes. The 'wrongful detention' claims were removed from the FAQ.

entries.new: Belarus waives visas for citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland among them — for stays of up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia) at any international road or rail crossing, under a regime that runs until December 31, 2026; CIS citizens and a list of bilateral partners enter visa-free, and a separate 30-day waiver covers 76 nationalities arriving and leaving through Minsk and five regional airports. US citizens and a few others can get a 30-day e-visa online; everyone else needs an embassy visa.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: It depends on your passport. Citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and the European microstates — enter visa-free for up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, and no more than 90 days in a calendar year) at any international road or rail crossing until December 31, 2026, and CIS citizens are visa-free under bilateral agreements. Many other nationalities (US, Canada, Japan and more) get 30 days visa-free only when flying in and out of Minsk National Airport. Everyone else needs a visa from a Belarusian embassy.
entries.new: It depends on your passport. Citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and the European microstates — enter visa-free for up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, and no more than 90 days in a calendar year) at any international road or rail crossing until December 31, 2026, and CIS citizens and a list of bilateral partners are visa-free too. 76 nationalities (Canada, Japan, Australia and more) get 30 days visa-free only when flying in and out through Minsk National Airport or five regional airports. US, Bolivian and Paraguayan citizens can apply online for a 30-day e-visa. Everyone else needs a visa from a Belarusian embassy.

Overstays are fined per day on departure.

entries.old: The Tunisian dinar is non-convertible — bringing dinars in or out of the country is prohibited. Declare foreign cash above the published threshold (roughly TND 20,000 equivalent) on arrival, and declare any amount you may want to take out again: re-exporting undeclared foreign currency is capped. Keep all exchange receipts to reconvert leftover dinars at departure.
entries.new: Any import or export of foreign currency worth TND 20,000 or more must be declared to Customs on entry, on exit and in transit. A non-resident can take out more than TND 5,000 of the foreign banknotes they brought in only if they declared them on entry, and at most TND 30,000 (above that, through a bank); the declaration is valid for 3 months and one trip, and can be made online in advance. Tunisian dinars may not be taken out of the country, so keep exchange receipts to reconvert leftover dinars before you leave.

entries.old: A passport valid 6 months with two blank pages, your yellow fever certificate, a return or onward ticket, and proof of accommodation and means for the stay. These apply to visa-free and visa-holding travelers alike.

entries.old: Yes. The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and the validity as 60 days; Iraq's portal says 30 days, so plan on 30. Apply at least 24 hours before departure — airlines check for the visa before boarding. Nationalities not eligible for the e-Visa apply at an Iraqi embassy.

entries.old: If you are from one of the roughly 100 visa-exempt countries — the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia, most of Latin America and others — you do not need a visa for stays of up to 90 days, but you must obtain an ETA-IL electronic travel authorization online before boarding. All other nationalities need a B/2 visitor visa from an Israeli embassy or consulate.
entries.new: If you are from one of the roughly 100 visa-exempt countries — the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia, most of Latin America and others — you do not need a visa for stays of up to 90 days, but you must obtain an ETA-IL electronic travel authorization online before boarding. Most other nationalities need a B/2 visitor visa from an Israeli embassy or consulate; citizens of Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Syria and Yemen are not admitted except with rare individual permission, and ordinary tourism is effectively closed to Afghan, Pakistani, Saudi, Somali and Sudanese passport holders.

entries.old: The official Japan eVisa at evisa.mofa.go.jp issues single-entry tourist visas to people who need a visa and legally reside in Australia, Brazil, Cambodia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Taiwan, the United Kingdom or the United States. entries.new: The official Japan eVisa at evisa.mofa.go.jp issues single-entry tourist visas to people who need a visa and legally reside in Australia, Brazil, Cambodia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Taiwan, the United Kingdom or the United States. Since 1 July 2026 a single-entry visa costs about 15,000 JPY; multiple-entry embassy visas cost about 30,000 JPY.

entries.old: A visitor's visa is issued free of charge on arrival for 30 days, on presentation of a passport valid 6 months beyond departure, an onward ticket and proof of funds. It can be extended month by month up to a total stay of about six months.
entries.new: A visitor's visa is issued free of charge on arrival for 30 days, on presentation of a passport valid 6 months beyond departure, an onward ticket and proof of funds. To stay longer, apply to the Immigration Department before it expires; no official source publishes the maximum total stay.
entries.note: The cited UK FCDO page says only to contact the Tonga Immigration Department to extend; it states no maximum. The 150-day extension (about six months in total) is withdrawn, matching the FAQ.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from a risk country
entries.new: No certificate is required for entry; vaccination is recommended for forested areas of Trinidad
entries.note: FAQ aligned with the vaccinations entry (WHO: no certificate requirement reported by Trinidad and Tobago).

entries.old: Tunisia lets citizens of a broad list of countries — the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, most of Europe and many Arab, African and Asian states — enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Nationalities outside the list apply for a consular visa; Israeli passport holders are not admitted.
entries.new: Tunisia lets citizens of a broad list of countries — every EU state except Cyprus, the UK, US, Canada, Japan, most of the rest of Europe, many Arab and African states and some Asian ones — enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Nationalities outside the list apply for a consular visa; Israeli passport holders are not admitted.

entries.old: Most Western tourists do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, and much of Europe, the Arab world, Africa and Latin America can stay visa-free for up to 90 days. Nationalities outside the exemption list — including most of South Asia and many African states — need a consular visa before travel.
entries.new: Most Western tourists do not. Citizens of the EU (except Cyprus), UK, US, Canada, Japan, and much of the rest of Europe, the Arab world and Africa, as well as Argentina, Brazil and Chile, can stay visa-free for up to 90 days. Nationalities outside the exemption list — including most of South Asia and many African states — need a consular visa before travel.

entries.old: conditional eVisa nationalities include Vietnam
entries.new: conditional eVisa nationalities include Egypt
entries.note: Vietnamese passport holders get the ordinary e-Visa, not the conditional one; Egypt is on the conditional list.

entries.old: The transit visa needs no invitation letter (3–7 days)
entries.new: The transit visa also needs a letter of invitation sponsored by the State Migration Service (up to 5 days per trip)
entries.note: The transit-visa fee notes and stay field say an invitation letter is required and the stay is up to 5 days.

entries.old: Embassy tourist visa or transit visa
entries.new: Embassy tourist visa, visa on arrival with a pre-approved invitation, or transit visa
entries.note: The visa-on-arrival type was described in the row notes and the FAQ but not linked from any passport row.

entries.old: The United Arab Emirates gives many passport holders a free visa on arrival — for most Western, Latin American and East Asian passports it allows 90 days within six months, for a smaller group 30 days — lets EU citizens stay visa-free for 90 days in any 180, and routes everyone else through pre-arranged tourist eVisas sponsored by airlines, hotels or UAE residents.
entries.new: The United Arab Emirates lets many passport holders in without arranging anything — a free visa on arrival for 90 days within six months for passports such as the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea (30 days for a smaller group), visa-free entry for most of Latin America and for China, and 90 days in any 180 visa-free for EU citizens — and routes everyone else through pre-arranged tourist eVisas sponsored by airlines, hotels or UAE residents.

entries.old: The United Kingdom now requires an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA, £20, valid 2 years) from all visa-exempt visitors — including US, EU and Commonwealth citizens — while visa nationals apply online for a Standard Visitor visa (£135, stays up to 6 months); only Irish citizens are exempt under the Common Travel Area.
entries.new: The United Kingdom now requires an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA, £20, valid 2 years) from all visa-exempt visitors — including US, EU, Canadian and Australian citizens — while visa nationals apply online for a Standard Visitor visa (£135, stays up to 6 months); only Irish citizens are exempt under the Common Travel Area.

entries.old: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires everyone else to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy — often with long interview wait times.
entries.new: The United States admits Visa Waiver Program nationals with an ESTA travel authorization ($40.27, valid 2 years) for stays up to 90 days, lets Canadians visit visa-free for up to 6 months, and requires everyone else to obtain a B1/B2 visitor visa ($185) at a US embassy — often with long interview wait times. Presidential proclamations of June and December 2025 suspend entry on visitor visas for citizens of more than 30 countries, with limited exemptions.

entries.old: Apply at e-visa.gov.uz with a passport scan and photo. The single-entry eVisa costs USD 20, is normally issued within two working days, and allows a 30-day stay within a 90-day validity window; double- and triple-entry versions cost USD 35 and USD 50.
entries.new: Apply at e-visa.gov.uz with a passport scan and photo. The single-entry eVisa costs USD 20, is normally issued within two working days, and allows a 30-day stay within a 90-day validity window; double-entry and multiple-entry versions cost USD 35 and USD 50.

entries.old: passport valid 6 months beyond departure
entries.new: passport valid for more than 6 months on arrival
entries.note: Matches the passport-validity rule.

entries.old: the Gulf states are visa-exempt
entries.new: most Gulf states are visa-exempt
entries.note: Bahrain is shown as needing a visitor e-Visa.

entries.new: Not yet in operation; no applications collected

entries.old: Zambia waived visas for 43 countries in 2022 and 53 more from January 2025, so 167 nationalities, including the US, UK and the EU, now enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 12 months. Most others can buy a visa on arrival or apply online, and about 50 nationalities need approval before travel; the KAZA UniVisa adds seamless travel with Zimbabwe around Victoria Falls.
entries.new: Zambia waived visas for 43 countries in 2022 and 53 more from January 2025, so 117 nationalities, including the US, UK and the EU, now enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 12 months. Of the rest, 28 nationalities can buy a visa on arrival or apply online, and about 50 need an eVisa approved before travel; the KAZA UniVisa adds seamless travel with Zimbabwe around Victoria Falls.

entries.old: null (not stated)

entries.old: Everyone needs a passport valid 6 months with two blank pages and a yellow fever certificate. eVisa applicants must also show a round-trip booking, accommodation and proof of means, and border officials may ask visa-free visitors for a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation too.
entries.new: Everyone needs a passport valid 6 months with two blank pages and a yellow fever certificate. eVisa applicants must also show a round-trip booking, accommodation and proof of means, and border officials may ask visa-free visitors for a return or onward ticket too.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. The only official statement about visa-free visitors (Canada: "Customs officials may ask you to show them a return or onward ticket") names the ticket, not proof of accommodation; accommodation is an eVisa document only (SME portal).

entries.old: No certificate is needed if you fly in directly from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean.
entries.new: WHO's risk list includes Trinidad and Tobago, so a Caribbean origin does not by itself exempt you.

entries.field: FAQ answer: how the 180 days are counted
entries.old: Most visa-waiver nationalities may stay up to 180 days in total within any one-year period — a rolling twelve months, not the calendar year. Citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay get up to 90 days under their own agreements. Longer stays require a residence permit from the migration authorities.
entries.new: Most visa-waiver nationalities may stay up to 180 days in total within one year. Citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay get up to 90 days under their own agreements. Longer stays require a residence permit from the migration authorities.
entries.note: Audit: MFA: visa-free nationals "can stay on the territory of the Republic of Armenia for no more than 180 days during one year". It does not say the year is a rolling twelve months rather than the calendar year; that clause is dropped. The 90-day nationalities match their rows.

entries.old: No official source states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to the Bahamas. Healthcare is paid for up front, so cover that includes medical evacuation is strongly advised.
entries.new: No official source states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to the Bahamas. The UK government says medical treatment can be expensive and that serious cases are transferred to Nassau, Freeport or Miami by air ambulance, so cover that includes medical evacuation is worth having.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. 'Healthcare is paid for up front' had no source (the cited immigration.gov.bs front page is silent). FCDO health page: 'Medical treatment is of a good standard but can be expensive... Serious cases are transferred to Nassau or Freeport – or Miami, USA – by air ambulance.' Text narrowed to that and the FCDO page cited (EN+AR).

entries.old: null (not published)

entries.new: 50 USD; notes: 'The 2016 circular does not print the amount; the immigration police's visa-on-arrival portal gives a visa fee of US$50, excluding processing fees, or as decided by the authority, paid at the Sonali Bank counter in the arrivals hall.'

entries.old: An embassy visa is the reliable route; Indian citizens holding a used multiple-entry Schengen, UK or US visa may qualify for the 30-day Minsk airport waiver. Verify with a Belarusian embassy first. Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen or EU-state visa, with a stamp showing it has been used, can instead enter visa-free for up to 30 days through Minsk National Airport or the five regional airports, with a confirmed departure within 30 days.
entries.new: Apply for a visa at a Belarusian embassy or consulate before travel. Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen or EU-state visa, with a stamp showing it has been used, can instead enter visa-free for up to 30 days through Minsk National Airport or the five regional airports, with a confirmed departure within 30 days.
entries.note: Audit: The airport list requires, for Indian citizens, a "valid multiple entry visa of EU or Schengen states with a mark of crossing the border"; UK and US visas do not qualify. The leftover sentence saying they do contradicted the sentence added on 2–3 Oct and is removed.

entries.field: FAQ: visa on arrival processing time
entries.old: Processing takes about 10 to 30 minutes at the border.
entries.new: Processing takes up to 10 minutes at border and airport posts, and up to 30 minutes at a migration office.
entries.note: Audit: DIGEMIG (Dec 2024 archive): 'PUESTO DE CONTROL MIGRATORIO FRONTERIZO TERRESTRE Y AEROPORTUARIO: El trámite tiene una duración de hasta 10 minutos. OFICINA CENTRAL O ADMINISTRACIONES DEPARTAMENTALES: ... hasta 30 minutos.' The 10–30 minute range at the border was not stated.

entries.old: 10–30 minutes

FIPA's visitor page still lists "Single-entry/exit or transit visa €31.00 / Multiple entry/exit or transit visa up to 90 days €57.00" next to notes about 2025; it is the older figure, so the embassies' current rate wins (newer) and FIPA is recorded as the conflict.

entries.field: FAQ: how to apply for the eVisa
entries.old: ... with a passport photo page scan, a recent photo, proof of onward travel and funds, and pay USD 80.90 by card. Processing is typically around 5 business days, but allow at least two weeks before travel.
entries.new: ... with a colour copy of your passport bio page and a recent photograph, and pay USD 80.90. The portal says processing takes up to 10 business days once your verified application is submitted, so apply well before travel.
entries.note: Audit: the portal lists only 'Photograph' and 'Passport Bio Page' as mandatory documents for adults and says 'Processing takes up to 10 business days once your verified application is submitted.' The Miami consulate also calls the eVisa requirements 'only passport and photo'. Onward-travel/funds, card payment and the 5-day figure had no source.

entries.old: Declare large sums of cash to customs on arrival — declarations can be made through the Customs.BN app or at the airport.
entries.new: The UK's travel advice says to declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty, through the Customs.BN app or on arrival at the airport.

The FCDO says only 'You must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty' and 'You can complete a declaration through the Customs.BN app or on arrival at the airport'; no official source tells travellers to declare large sums of cash. Fees: BND20.00 / BND30.00'. Row note and the Australians FAQ (and Arabic) now say single or multiple entry.

entries.old: The DRC committed to waive visas for Ugandan citizens by 31 August 2026, reciprocating Uganda’s January 2024 waiver for Congolese citizens (Uganda’s embassy in Kinshasa, 11 May 2026), and press reports since June 2026 describe a DGM directive exempting Ugandans for stays of up to 90 days. No official DRC text of that exemption is published, so carry the eVisa or an embassy visa unless the DGM or a DRC embassy confirms the waiver.
entries.new: The DRC committed to fast-tracking procedures for a reciprocal visa waiver for Ugandan citizens by 31 August 2026, following Uganda's January 2024 waiver for Congolese citizens (Uganda's embassy in Kinshasa, 11 May 2026). No official DRC text of that waiver is published, so carry the eVisa or an embassy visa unless the DGM or a DRC embassy confirms the waiver.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. Uganda's embassy says only that the DRC 'committed to fast-tracking procedures for a reciprocal visa waiver for Ugandan nationals by 31st August 2026'; the clause on press reports of a 90-day DGM directive rested on a news site, not an official source, and is dropped. Requirement (eVisa) unchanged.

entries.old: No official source we found states a proof-of-funds requirement or a minimum amount for tourists.
entries.new: No minimum amount is published. Canada's travel advice says you may need to prove adequate funds for the duration of your stay when you enter, and give the address where you will be staying.
entries.note: Audit: Canada: 'When you enter the Dominican Republic, you may need to be able to prove adequate funds for the duration of your stay. You will also need to provide the address where you will be staying during your travel.'

entries.old: recommended: No yellow fever certificate is required to enter Ecuador

entries.old: No official source states a travel insurance requirement for entering Eritrea. Medical facilities are very limited and serious cases need evacuation abroad, so cover that includes medical evacuation is advisable.

Public hospitals in other towns are often poorly equipped. entries.old: 6-months-on-arrival: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Fiji. This is enforced by airlines at check-in as well as by immigration.

entries.old: Foreign currency must be declared to customs on arrival, and foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border. GPS devices are held by customs until you leave, and books, films and data storage devices may be inspected; material judged anti-government, religious or pornographic is confiscated and can lead to imprisonment.
entries.new: Foreign currency must be declared to customs on arrival, and foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border. GPS devices are held by customs until you leave. Customs officers confiscate literature or media judged anti-government, subversive or pornographic, and further severe penalties, including imprisonment, are possible; the UK government advises against bringing Korean-language or religious material.
entries.note: Audit: FCDO: officers "will confiscate any literature or media deemed to have an anti-government message or deemed subversive or pornographic"; religious content appears only in "Avoid bringing books or other written material in the Korean language, including anything with religious content". The 2-3 October text put "religious" in the confiscation list and said books, films and storage devices "may be inspected", which FCDO does not state. Narrowed to the FCDO wording.

entries.old: No official source states an onward or return ticket requirement for entry to Pakistan. The tourist eVisa asks for a hotel booking, and airlines may ask to see a return booking.
entries.new: No official source states an onward or return ticket requirement for entry to Pakistan. The tourist eVisa asks for a hotel booking.
entries.note: Audit: "Airlines may ask to see a return booking" has no official source; the tourist-visa page lists only photograph, passport and hotel booking. Clause dropped.

entries.old: Travellers may bring foreign currency notes into Pakistan without limit. Pakistani rupees are limited to PKR 10,000 per person in or out (PKR 3,000 to or from India). Taking foreign currency out is capped per visit at USD 10,000 for adults, USD 5,000 for ages 5–18 and USD 1,000 for children under 5 (or the equivalent).
entries.new: Travellers may bring foreign currency notes into Pakistan without limit. Pakistani rupees are limited to PKR 10,000 per person in or out (PKR 3,000 to or from India). A general permission lets anyone take foreign currency out up to USD 10,000 per visit for adults, USD 5,000 for ages 5–18 and USD 1,000 for children under 5 (or the equivalent); visitors not ordinarily resident in Pakistan may also take out the unspent foreign currency they brought in, if their stay has not exceeded three months.
entries.note: Audit: SBP Chapter 18 sets the USD 10,000 / 5,000 / 1,000 limits as a "general permission to any person to take out" (F.E.1/2015), and separately permits "Any person not ordinarily resident in Pakistan, to take out of Pakistan the unspent amount of foreign currency brought by him into Pakistan, provided the period of his continuous stay in Pakistan does not exceed three months". Calling the limits a cap overstated it for visitors; text narrowed.

entries.old: Risk zones listed as Brazil (Amazonas, Minas Gerais, São Paulo, Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima), Colombia (Caquetá, Huila, Nariño, Putumayo, Vaupés, Tolima) and Peru (Huánuco, Junín, Madre de Dios, San Martín, Ucayali)

entries.old: No official source states an onward or return ticket requirement for entry to Peru, but airlines and immigration officers frequently ask for proof of onward or return travel. Carry a booking that leaves Peru within your permitted stay.
entries.new: No official source states an onward or return ticket requirement for entry to Peru. Canada's travel advice says officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket, so carry a booking that leaves Peru within your permitted stay.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. 'Airlines and immigration officers frequently ask' had no source (the cited Migraciones front page is silent). Canada (updated 11 Sep 2026): 'Customs officials may ask you to show them: a return or onward ticket'. Narrowed to that and Canada cited (EN+AR).

entries.old: No official source states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Peru, but officers may ask about your means of support, itinerary and accommodation when deciding how many days to grant.
entries.new: No official source states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for Peru. Canada's travel advice says officials may ask for proof that you have a place to stay and sufficient funds for the duration of your stay.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. 'Officers may ask about your means of support ... when deciding how many days to grant' had no source. Canada: officials may ask for 'proof that you have a place to stay' and 'proof of sufficient funds for the duration of your stay'. Narrowed and Canada cited (EN+AR).

entries.old: Visa-free. Qatar Tourism's nationality checker lists Uzbek citizens as able to enter without a visa (or to apply for a Hayya A1 visa in advance), and its list of nationalities that need a tourist visa does not include them; the passport must be valid for at least three months on arrival. No official source we could read publishes the length of the visa-free stay for this nationality; the immigration officer sets it on arrival.
entries.new: Visa-free. Qatar Tourism's list of nationalities that need a tourist visa or pay for one on arrival does not include Uzbekistan, and the page says the other nationalities receive free entry on arrival. Its nationality checker gives no answer for Uzbek citizens unless they hold a visa or residence permit for the Schengen area, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia or New Zealand, in which case it says they enter visa-free with a passport valid for at least three months on arrival and a confirmed hotel booking. No official source we could read publishes the length of the visa-free stay for this nationality; the immigration officer sets it on arrival.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. The checker's nationality dropdown codes Uzbekistan 'A3/uz', so the 'Enter visa-free OR apply now for a Hayya A1 Entry Visa' result (code A1-3) never shows for it; only the Schengen/UK/US/CA/AU/NZ-residence path returns 'Enter visa-free ... confirmed hotel booking on arrival'. The visa-free requirement still rests on Uzbekistan's absence from the page's tourist-visa list; the note now says exactly that.

Only Canada (rank 5) counts from departure from Congo. Hierarchy: embassies win. Text unchanged.

entries.old: Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa, and UK, US or EU permanent residents, are eligible for the Saudi tourist visa on arrival whatever their nationality. entries.new: Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa that has been used at least once — it must carry an entry stamp from the issuing country; digital entry stamps are not accepted — and holders of a UK, US or EU permanent residence permit are eligible for the Saudi tourist visa on arrival whatever their nationality.
entries.note: Audit: wrong — the used-at-least-once condition is still stated. Visit Saudi's visa-requirements content (bin/api/v2/evisa/config, the data behind the cited page), visa-on-arrival requirements: "Your visa must have been used at least once and have an entry stamp from the issuing country (Digital entry stamp are not accepted)"; residents "must hold a permanent residence permit from ... the U.K., U.S. or EU". The FAQ is silent on the condition, and silence is not a statement.

entries.old: GCC residents are eligible for the Saudi tourist visa whatever their nationality, issued as an eVisa or through an embassy; the Visa Requirements page checks eVisa eligibility.
entries.new: GCC residents whose residence permit is valid for at least three months beyond the date of entry are eligible for the Saudi tourist visa whatever their nationality, issued as an eVisa or through an embassy; the Visa Requirements page checks eVisa eligibility.
entries.note: Audit: wrong — the residence-validity condition is still stated. Visit Saudi eVisa requirements for GCC residents: "You must provide a residency visa from one of the GCC countries with a minimum validity of at least three months beyond the date of entry into Saudi." The FAQ omits it; silence is not a statement.

entries.field: FAQ: visa on arrival with a Western visa
entries.old: Yes. Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa, and UK, US or EU permanent residents, are eligible for a visa on arrival whether or not their nationality is on the eVisa list — a route often used by Indian, Pakistani and Filipino travelers. Older guidance required the visa to have been used once; the current official FAQ does not say so. Confirm current conditions on visa.visitsaudi.com before flying.
entries.new: Yes. Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa that has been used at least once (with an entry stamp from the issuing country — digital stamps are not accepted), and holders of a UK, US or EU permanent residence permit, are eligible for a visa on arrival whether or not their nationality is on the eVisa list — a route often used by Indian, Pakistani and Filipino travelers. Confirm current conditions on visa.visitsaudi.com before flying.
entries.note: Audit: wrong. Visit Saudi's visa-requirements content (bin/api/v2/evisa/config, the data behind the cited page), visa-on-arrival requirements: "Your visa must have been used at least once and have an entry stamp from the issuing country (Digital entry stamp are not accepted)"; residents "must hold a permanent residence permit from ... the U.K., U.S. or EU". The FAQ is silent on the condition, and silence is not a statement.

Indian citizens holding a valid US, UK or Schengen visa (or a UK/US/EU residence permit) can apply for the tourist eVisa or get a visa on arrival; all other Indian passport holders need an embassy visa or travel under the work or Umrah regimes.

entries.old: Solomon Islands no longer issues visitor permits on arrival: every visitor must apply online before travel and show the grant letter at the border. Former on-arrival nationalities, including the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand and Japan, can apply for a free 30-day Tourist Permit (USD 50 lodgement fee); EU, Chinese, Hong Kong and Emirati citizens get a fee-free mutual exemption; everyone else needs the 3-month Tourist Visa (USD 50 plus USD 50 lodgement).
entries.new: Solomon Islands no longer issues visitor permits on arrival: every visitor must apply online before travel and show the grant letter at the border. The standard route is the 3-month Tourist Visa (USD 50 plus USD 50 lodgement); the Immigration Division also offers a free 30-day, single-entry Tourist Permit (USD 50 lodgement fee) but does not say which nationalities may use it. EU, Chinese, Hong Kong and Emirati citizens get a fee-free mutual exemption.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. The Immigration Division's '30 days - Tourist permit' page says only 'This visa is for tourist who intend to visit Solomon Islands for short stay holidays...' and 'This tourist permit is free. However, an online lodgement fee of $50 USD will be charged'; it names no eligible nationalities, so the claim that it is for former on-arrival nationalities and that everyone else needs the Tourist Visa was unsourced. Narrowed (EN+AR).

entries.old: Yes, in the sense that everyone must now be approved online before travel: Solomon Islands no longer issues permits on arrival. If your country used to get one (the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan and many Commonwealth and Pacific countries), apply for the free 30-day Tourist Permit, paying the USD 50 lodgement fee. EU, Chinese, Hong Kong and Emirati citizens apply for a fee-free mutual exemption. Everyone else applies for the Tourist Visa.
entries.new: Yes, in the sense that everyone must now be approved online before travel: Solomon Islands no longer issues permits on arrival. Apply for the 3-month Tourist Visa (USD 50 plus USD 50 lodgement) or the free 30-day Tourist Permit (USD 50 lodgement fee); the Immigration Division does not say which nationalities may use the permit. EU, Chinese, Hong Kong and Emirati citizens apply for a fee-free mutual exemption.
entries.note: Audit: overreach. The Immigration Division's '30 days - Tourist permit' page says only 'This visa is for tourist who intend to visit Solomon Islands for short stay holidays...' and 'This tourist permit is free. However, an online lodgement fee of $50 USD will be charged'; it names no eligible nationalities, so the claim that it is for former on-arrival nationalities and that everyone else needs the Tourist Visa was unsourced. Narrowed (EN+AR).

entries.new: In Somaliland, cash or travellers cheques worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared. No official threshold is published for the rest of Somalia.

The Central Bank's Department of Foreign Exchange (dfe.lk) adds that arriving travellers should declare any foreign currency notes over USD 10,000 they intend to take out again, and that Sri Lankan rupees carried in or out are limited to LKR 20,000.

The 2 October pass removed the figures as unstated, but the Central Bank's Department of Foreign Exchange states them: "a person shall make a declaration to the Sri Lanka Customs if that amount exceeds USD 15,000 ... or if he/she arriving in Sri Lanka intends to take back foreign currency notes exceeding USD 10,000" and "may take out of, or bring into Sri Lanka ... Sri Lanka currency up to the value of Sri Lanka Rupees 20,000". (The pre-2 Oct USD 5,000 export figure was also wrong; the source says USD 10,000.) Cited to the CBSL glossary ("Declaration to the Department of Customs where foreign exchange exceeds USD 15,000"), because dfe.lk (https://www.dfe.lk/web/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=387&Itemid=724&lang=en, linked from cbsl.gov.lk as its Department of Foreign Exchange) is not yet in data/official-hosts.json.

entries.old: Nearly every government advises against ALL travel to Afghanistan. Terrorist attacks — including against foreigners and religious minorities — kidnapping and arbitrary detention are real risks anywhere in the country, and no embassy can offer meaningful help on the ground.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel to Afghanistan, even with an organised tour group. The security situation is volatile, there is a high risk of foreigners being detained or kidnapped, terrorists often target places frequented by foreign nationals, and in-person consular help is not possible.
entries.note: 'Nearly every government' and 'religious minorities' are not on the cited page. FCDO: 'advises against all travel to Afghanistan, even if you are part of an organised tour group. EN+AR.

entries.field: Iranian row: visa waiver for Schengen/UK/US visa holders
entries.old: A short-stay visa is required. Apply online through Albania's e-Visa portal (e-visa.al) or at an Albanian embassy; holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen, UK or US visa may instead enter visa-free for up to 90 days.
entries.new: A short-stay visa is required in all cases: apply online through Albania's e-Visa portal (e-visa.al) or at an Albanian embassy. The visa-free entry Albania grants to holders of Schengen, EU, UK or US visas and residence permits does not apply to Iranian citizens. The visa fee for these passport holders is EUR 35 (Council of Ministers Decision No. 329 of 29.05.2024).
entries.note: MFA: 'This exemption does not apply to Iranian nationals, who are required to obtain a visa in all cases.' The row told Iranians they could use the waiver. Fee from the e-Visa portal's fee table.

entries.old: Northern cities such as Algiers, Oran and Constantine are generally safe with normal precautions. Western governments advise against travel near the Libyan, Malian and Nigerien borders and parts of the Sahara — far-south desert tourism is done with accredited agencies, which the visa-on-arrival scheme requires anyway.

The UK advises against all travel within 30 km of Algeria's borders with Libya, Mauritania, Mali and Niger and parts of the Tunisian border, and against all but essential travel near the rest of the border with Tunisia — far-south desert tourism is done with accredited agencies, which the visa-on-arrival scheme requires anyway.
entries.note: FCDO: 'advises against all travel to within 30km of Algeria's borders with: Libya, Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Tunisia – in the provinces of Illizi and Ouargla and in the Chaambi mountains area' and all but essential travel within 30km of the rest of the Tunisian border. Mauritania and Tunisia were missing.

entries.old: Andorra is one of the safest places in Europe, with very little crime. The real risks are alpine ones: winter driving, fast-changing mountain weather and ski injuries.
entries.new: Street crime is rare, though you should still look after your belongings. Although Andorra has no recent history of terrorism, attacks cannot be ruled out. If you plan to ski, check the weather and avalanche safety advice before you go.
entries.note: 'One of the safest places in Europe', winter driving and ski injuries are not on the FCDO pages; the cited front page has no safety detail. FCDO safety page: 'Street crime is rare, but you should: take care of your personal belongings'; 'Although there's no recent history of terrorism in Andorra, attacks cannot be ruled out'; 'If you plan to ski in Andorra, before you travel check: weather conditions; safety advice, including protecting yourself against avalanches'. Re-cited. EN+AR.

entries.old: You apply online at smevisa.gov.ao and receive a pre-approval letter, usually within about 3–10 business days. You board with the letter and the visa itself is stamped on arrival at Luanda or another international entry point; the fee is Kz 36,600, paid in cash at the border.

entries.old: Luanda is generally manageable but has significant street crime. Keep valuables out of sight and use trusted drivers at night. Roads outside the cities are poor, landmines remain a hazard off marked routes in some rural provinces, and the interior of Cabinda province should be avoided due to a lingering separatist insurgency.
entries.new: Luanda has a high level of crime, some of it violent: avoid walking around, especially alone or after dark, and keep valuables out of sight in traffic. Roads outside the main cities can be poor, and the UK advises against all but essential travel to Cabinda Province, except Cabinda city, because separatist groups have attacked foreigners and there is a risk of kidnap.
entries.note: FCDO: "There is a high level of crime in Luanda, some of it violent"; "FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cabinda Province, except to Cabinda city ... separatist groups carrying out targeted attacks on foreigners and the risk of kidnap". The FCDO pages no longer mention landmines, and "generally manageable" is not stated.

entries.old: Visa-free entry under the 2023 decree is for tourism only — 30 days per visit and 90 days per calendar year. Border officers expect a return ticket, proof of accommodation and your yellow fever card, so keep all three to hand.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged one year and over arriving from — or having recently transited — a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. No vaccination is required if you fly in directly from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean.
entries.new: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers over one year of age arriving directly from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, or who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in such a country; the vaccination must have been given at least 10 days before arrival. Travelers arriving from Trinidad and Tobago are exempt.
entries.note: Immigration Department: 'Travellers over 1 year of age arriving directly from a country with risk...'; 'transited more than 12 hours through an airport'; 'must be vaccinated at least 10 days before entering'; 'Trinidad and Tobago: Effective January 2014, proof... no longer required'. 'Recently transited' sharpened to >12 h; the unsourced 'no vaccination... from Europe, North America or the rest of the Caribbean' replaced by the stated exemption. EN+AR.

entries.old: Visitors must hold a return or onward ticket and give the address where they are staying; officers set the length of stay on that basis.
entries.new: Visitors must hold a valid return ticket or other means of leaving the Bahamas and present a completed immigration disembarkation/embarkation card at the border.
entries.note: Immigration Act s.22 criteria as listed: 'possess a valid return ticket/ means of departing The Bahamas'; 'present a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card'. 'Officers set the length of stay on that basis' is not stated; narrowed. EN+AR.

entries.old: The Family Islands have lower crime rates, but violent crime and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, occur in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama. Stay in the main tourist areas on foot and avoid unlit areas after dark. Water sports are poorly regulated, so take care renting jet skis, and never swim in water baited for sharks.
entries.new: Violent crime and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, occur in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama. Do not go on foot outside the main tourist areas and beaches, avoid unlit areas and travel in groups after dusk. Water sports are poorly regulated, so take care renting jet skis, and never swim in water baited for sharks.
entries.note: 'The Family Islands have lower crime rates' is not on the FCDO page. FCDO: 'violent crimes and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama... do not go on foot outside the main tourist areas and beaches... Avoid unlit areas, and travel in groups after dusk'; 'water sports industry... poorly regulated'; 'Never go into water that has been baited.' EN+AR.

entries.note: NPRA two-week eVisa page: 'Processing Time — Issuance 1 working day' (not 3–5 business days); 'Extension fee 25 BHD (for 14 days)', extension application 'at the service center only'.

entries.old: Residents of other GCC states can generally apply for a Bahrain eVisa (or obtain a visa on arrival) regardless of nationality. Confirm eligibility on evisa.gov.bh.
entries.new: Residents of other GCC states, whatever their nationality, can apply online from outside Bahrain for a two-week single-entry eVisa (BHD 5 application plus BHD 5 issuance fee), attaching their GCC residence permit with a return visa valid for at least 3 months; issuance takes one working day.
entries.note: NPRA GCC-resident two-week eVisa page: issued 'to GCC residents'; documents: passport valid more than 6 months and 'A clear copy of the visitor's resident permit with a valid return visa valid for at least 3 months'; 'Issuance 1 working day'; fees BHD 5 + BHD 5. It does not mention a visa on arrival for GCC residents; that clause is removed.

entries.old: {"requirement": "embassy-visa", "maxStayDays": null, "visaTypes": ["tourist-visa"], "notes": "Apply for a visa before travel through a Bangladeshi embassy or high commission, starting the application on the official portal visa.gov.bd. If you are traveling from a country where Bangladesh has no mission, immigration may instead grant a 30-day visa on arrival."}
entries.new: {"requirement": "visa-free", "maxStayDays": 90, "notes": "Visa-free for up to 90 days: the immigration police (Special Branch) eligibility checker states that no visa is required to enter and stay in Bangladesh for up to 90 days. Bangladesh's published list of visa-exemption agreements does not name this country, so this is a unilateral exemption; the checker carries no date, and immigration officers decide entry.", "source": {"url": "https://immi.specialbranch.gov.bd/Land-Permit-Eligibility", "name": "Immigration, Special Branch of Bangladesh Police — landing permit / visa-on-arrival eligibility checker", "type": "government", "lastVerified": "2026-10-03", "lastChanged": "2026-10-03"}}
entries.note: Settles the open issue. The Special Branch eligibility checker (the immigration police, rank 2) gives Ghana code 2: 'No visa is required to enter and to stay for not more than 90 days in Bangladesh.' The embassy-visa row rested only on visa.gov.bd's fee schedule, which prices a visa for every nationality and does not say one is required, and the 2016 circular does not name Ghana. Explicit statement wins: visa-free 90, as already done for BB, BT, FJ, GD, JM, KN and TT on the same basis.

entries.field: Embassy-visa rows where the checker allows a landing permit / visa on arrival (47 rows)
entries.old: no mention of the checker
entries.new: note adds the checker allowance; source = Special Branch checker
entries.note: Settles the corpus-wide question left open in reports4/f3: the checker's code 8 reads 'Visa is required to travel to Bangladesh. Please obtain your visa from nearest Bangladeshi mission. You are also allowed to obtain landing permit or visa-on-arrival for maximum 30 days' (code 7: 15 days; code 6: mission visa and 30-day landing permit both free). Its primary statement is that a visa is required, so requirement stays embassy-visa (the reading that cannot strand a traveller); the allowance is now stated in every such row, as was already done for LC, VC, SB, PG and VU.

entries.old: Chinese citizens enter without a visa under the bilateral waiver agreement, commonly for up to 30 days. Confirm the current allowance before booking.
entries.new: Chinese citizens holding ordinary passports enter without a visa for stays of up to 30 days under the China–Barbados mutual visa exemption agreement, in force since 1 June 2017. A longer stay, study or work needs a visa before travel.
entries.note: Barbados MFA list says only "No Visa required ... Visa abolition agreement established on May 27, 2014" with no stay for Chinese nationals; the Chinese embassy notice states "a period of stay not exceeding thirty (30) days from the date of their entry". 30 days now sourced; hedge removed. Not a conflict (the Barbados list is silent on the length).

entries.new: null (more than 90 days; no fixed figure)
entries.note: MFA (Visa Regulations, Decree No. 464 of 14 Sep 2026): "D – long-term visa, valid for the period exceeding 90 days with the right to stay in the Republic of Belarus up to 90 days". No 365-day figure is stated. Type C ("valid for up to 90 days"), processing ("5 working days (as a matter of urgency — within 2 working days)") and the EUR 60 fee (/en/visa/stavki/: "60 Euro (for all types of visa with any number of entries)") are unchanged under the new regulations.

entries.old: Visa-free under CIS-era bilateral agreements — typically up to 90 days per year; register with the migration authorities if staying more than 10 days.
entries.new: Visa-free (on the MFA's general visa-free list). The list gives no stay limit, so Belarusian law applies: a visa-free stay may not exceed 90 days in a calendar year unless a treaty sets another limit (Law No. 105-Z, Art. 39). Register with the migration authorities within 10 days of arrival.
entries.note: maxStayDays 90 kept, now resting on Law 105-Z Art. 39: the stay of a foreigner who arrived visa-free "не может превышать девяноста суток в календарном году, если иное не определено ... международными договорами". The MFA list names these countries without a stay. The old note called the agreements "CIS-era" and hedged "typically". Registration: MFA /en/visa/registration/ (within ten days; Kazakhstan, Ukraine and others up to 30 days without registration).

entries.old: Southern Benin, including Cotonou, is generally calm apart from petty crime, but the northern border areas — including Pendjari and W national parks — carry a serious risk of terrorist attack and kidnapping. Check advisories and avoid the far north.
entries.new: Southern Benin, including Cotonou, is calmer, but street crime, theft and mugging are common in Cotonou and carjacking is a risk on roads outside towns. In the north the FCDO advises against all travel to the W and Pendjari national parks, their hunting zones and the area between Park W and the Niger border, because of terrorist attacks and kidnapping, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the Alibori and Atacora departments and to the area between the RNIE 2 highway (Tchaourou–Malanville) and the Nigerian border.
entries.note: FCDO Benin (updated 15 Dec 2025): advises against all travel to Parc du W, the Mékrou and Djona hunting zones, the area between Park W and the Niger border and Pendjari National Park; against all but essential travel to the rest of Alibori and Atacora and to the area between the RNIE 2 (Tchaourou–Malanville) and the Nigerian border. Safety page: 'Street crime, including theft and mugging, is common in Cotonou'. The previous text ('avoid the far north', 'calm apart from petty crime') understated both.

entries.old: The south — Cotonou, Ouidah, Porto-Novo, Abomey and the coast — is generally calm apart from petty crime. The far north along the Burkina Faso and Niger borders, including the national parks, is high-risk and best avoided; check current advisories before traveling.
entries.new: The south — Cotonou, Ouidah, Porto-Novo, Abomey and the coast — is calmer, though street crime, theft and mugging are common in Cotonou. In the north the FCDO advises against all travel to the W and Pendjari national parks and nearby border areas, and against all but essential travel to the rest of the Alibori and Atacora departments and to the strip between the RNIE 2 highway and the Nigerian border; check current advisories before traveling.
entries.note: Repetition of the safety correction (FCDO zones).

entries.old: Bhutan is one of Asia's safest destinations, with very low crime. The practical risks are altitude on treks, winding mountain roads and stray dogs — not people.
entries.new: Australia advises normal safety precautions in Bhutan. The crime rate is low and violent crime is rare, though petty crime such as theft, pickpocketing and bag snatching can happen. Altitude sickness is a risk above 2,500 m, and flooding and landslides can disrupt transport in the June–September monsoon.
entries.note: Smartraveller: 'Exercise normal safety precautions'; 'Bhutan's crime rate is low. Violent crime is rare, but petty crime, such as burglary, theft, pickpocketing and bag snatching, can happen'; altitude sickness above 2500m; flooding and landslides June–September. 'One of Asia's safest destinations' and 'stray dogs' are not on the cited page.

entries.old: Bolivia is not a violent-crime destination for most visitors, but three things need care: altitude, road travel, and political blockades (bloqueos) that can close highways and airports at short notice. Express kidnapping and fake-police scams occur in La Paz and Santa Cruz. Use only radio taxis booked through your hotel.
entries.new: Bolivia needs care with altitude, road travel and protests: a State of Emergency is in force over roadblocks, which can close highways at short notice, and the UK advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba. Express kidnapping and criminals posing as police are a risk, and taxi robberies have risen in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque — order radio taxis by phone.
entries.note: FCDO: 'advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba Department'; 'A State of Emergency has been declared in Bolivia, giving police and armed forces powers to remove roadblocks'; express kidnapping (not limited to La Paz and Santa Cruz); 'Criminals impersonating Police Officers'; taxi robberies 'in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque'; order radio taxis by phone. The Chapare advice and State of Emergency were missing; 'not a violent-crime destination' and 'airports' are not in the source.

entries.old: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but healthcare for visitors is expensive and public coverage does not apply — comprehensive medical coverage is strongly recommended. [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada.html]
entries.new: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement for visitors, and no official source we could read makes it one. Medical treatment can be very expensive and there are no special arrangements for visitors, so cover for local treatment and medical evacuation is worth having.
entries.note: IRCC's Visit Canada page states no insurance rule (not-stated since 2026-10-03). FCDO health: 'Medical treatment can be very expensive. There are no special arrangements for British visitors'; 'check that... you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation'. 'Public coverage does not apply' narrowed to what FCDO says; required:false kept. Re-cited. EN+AR.

entries.old: Canada is one of the safest countries in the world for visitors, with low crime nationwide. Take normal precautions in big-city downtown areas at night, and prepare properly for winter driving and remote wilderness travel.
entries.new: Take ordinary precautions against petty crime: do not leave bags unattended and keep luggage out of sight in cars. Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Canada. Winter storms, including freezing rain and blizzards, make driving dangerous in many areas from November to April; wildfires are a risk especially in summer, and emergency help is limited in remote Arctic areas.
entries.note: 'One of the safest countries in the world... low crime nationwide' is on no FCDO page; the cited front page has no safety detail. FCDO safety page: 'Take precautions to protect yourself from petty crime, including: not leaving your bag or luggage unattended; keeping luggage out of sight in cars'; 'Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Canada'; 'Winter storms, including freezing rain, blizzards and hail, are frequent... from November to April. They can make driving conditions dangerous'; wildfires; Arctic: 'Emergency medical assistance and search and rescue are limited'. Re-cited. EN+AR.

entries.old: Most tourist areas — Bogotá, Medellín, Cartagena, the Coffee Axis — are fine with sensible precautions, but robbery and drink-spiking scams do target tourists, and some border and rural regions remain no-go areas. Avoid displaying valuables, use app-based taxis and check regional advice before traveling off the beaten path.
entries.new: Pickpocketing, mugging and armed robbery are a problem in the major cities, including Bogotá, Medellín, Cali and the Caribbean coast, and criminals use drugs such as scopolamine to rob victims, as well as dating apps to lure lone travellers; express kidnappings happen in unlicensed taxis, so use licensed phone or app taxis. The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of the country, including all of Norte de Santander and Arauca, much of the Pacific coast and Chocó, Guaviare, parts of Caquetá, Meta, Cauca and Putumayo, and areas near the Venezuelan and Ecuadorian borders.
entries.note: FCDO Colombia (updated 23 Sep 2026): advises against all but essential travel to all of Norte de Santander and Arauca, Chocó (except Quibdó, Nuquí, Bahía Solano, Capurganá), western Valle del Cauca, parts of Nariño, Córdoba, Antioquia and Bolívar, Guaviare, parts of Caquetá and southern Meta, Cauca (except Popayán), parts of Putumayo and within 5 km of the Venezuelan and Ecuadorian borders. Safety page: 'Pickpocketing, mugging and armed robbery are a problem, especially in major cities'; scopolamine; dating-app lures; express kidnappings in unlicensed taxis. The previous text said tourist areas are 'fine with sensible precautions' and called the zones 'no-go', which the FCDO does not.

entries.old: Visa-free for a shorter stay (second-group nationality, typically up to 30 days on entry, extendable in-country). Groupings change periodically. Confirm with a consulate before booking.
entries.new: Visa-free for up to 30 days (second-group nationality), extendable in-country up to 90 days in total; the passport must be valid for at least 90 days. Hondurans aged 18 and over must also show a police certificate from their country of origin (no apostille needed) proving they have no criminal record; air transit passengers are exempt.
entries.note: DGME directives Tercero VII: Hondurans, though in the second group, 'deberán presentar como requisito de ingreso, el certificado de antecedentes policiales, sin apostillar ... a partir de los 18 años de edad'; not required for 'tránsito aéreo'. Second group: 'HASTA LOS TREINTA DÍAS NATURALES (prorrogables hasta un total de noventa días naturales)', passport 90 days.

entries.field: FAQ: entry with a US or Schengen visa
entries.old: Often yes. Nationals of visa-required countries who hold a valid multiple-entry visa or residence permit for the United States, Canada or the Schengen area can generally enter Costa Rica without a consular visa, for up to 30 days (or until the visa expires, if sooner). Confirm the current rules for your nationality with a Costa Rican consulate before booking.
entries.new: Often yes. Nationals of visa-required countries can enter Costa Rica without a Costa Rican visa for up to 30 days, never beyond the visa's expiry, if they hold a valid multiple-entry US or Canadian visa (not a C1, C2 or C3 transit visa) or US or Canadian residence, a multiple-entry Schengen C or D visa, or a residence permit from the UK, the EU, Iceland, Norway or Switzerland valid for at least 90 more days. Confirm the current rules for your nationality with a Costa Rican consulate before booking.
entries.note: Aligns the FAQ with the waiver text and the DGME directives: adds UK, EU, Iceland, Norway and Switzerland residence permits (valid 90 days more) and the C1/C2/C3 exclusion.

entries.old: Cuba runs on cash for visitors. Cards issued by US banks do not work at all, and other foreign cards are unreliable. Bring euros, Canadian dollars, pounds or US dollars in cash and change what you need. Some hotels and state shops take payment only by card in foreign currency, so carry both if you can. (cardsAccepted limited)
entries.new: Cuba runs on cash for visitors. Cuba's Central Bank has announced that international cards such as Visa and Mastercard are no longer accepted, and you cannot withdraw cash from ATMs with a foreign card; the other way to pay is a Cuban prepaid card. Bring enough US dollars or euros in cash for the whole stay and for emergencies, and change money only at official exchange points. (cardsAccepted rare)
entries.note: Settles the clash with tips[bring-cash]. FCDO (updated 25 Sep 2026): 'The Cuban Central Bank has announced that international cards such as Visa and Mastercard are no longer accepted in Cuba. Available payment methods include cash and Cuban prepaid cards (CLASICA card). You will not be able to withdraw cash through ATMs with an international card... US dollars and euros are widely accepted'; 'It is illegal to exchange money anywhere other than' official points. 'Other foreign cards are unreliable' and 'some hotels... take payment only by card' contradicted it. EN+AR.

entries.old: Governments advise against all travel to eastern DRC — North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri, where the M23 conflict and other armed groups are active — and to much of the rest of the country. Kinshasa itself sees high crime and occasional unrest; travel with experienced local support.
entries.new: Governments advise against all travel to eastern DRC — North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri, where the M23 conflict and other armed groups are active — and the UK also advises against all travel to Haut-Uélé, Maniema, Tanganyika and Haut-Lomami provinces, the Kwamouth territory of Mai-Ndombe and within 50 km of the Central African Republic border. Kinshasa itself sees high crime and occasional unrest; travel with experienced local support.
entries.note: FCDO (updated 16 September 2026) names the provinces under all-travel advice: "Haut-Uélé and Ituri, ... North Kivu, South Kivu, Maniema, Tanganyika, Haut-Lomami", plus "within 50km of the border with the Central African Republic" and "the Kwamouth territory of Mai-Ndombe Province". "Much of the rest of the country" overstated it: Kinshasa and most western and southern provinces are not under all-travel advice.

entries.old: Denmark has very low crime and consistently ranks among the world's safest countries. The main tourist nuisances are pickpocketing around Copenhagen Central Station, Strøget and Nørreport, and bicycle traffic — look both ways before crossing cycle lanes.
entries.new: Crime levels are generally low, but pickpockets and bag-snatchers operate in crowded areas, mainly in Copenhagen: the central station, Nørreport, Strøget, Nyhavn, Christiania and Kastrup Airport. Take extra care in Christiania and Nørrebro late at night. Cyclists often have the right of way, so check cycle lanes before crossing or turning.
entries.note: 'Consistently ranks among the world's safest countries' is on no FCDO page; the cited front page has no safety detail. FCDO safety page: 'Crime levels are generally low, but pickpockets and bag-snatchers operate in crowded areas, mainly in Copenhagen'; lists the central station, Nørreport, Strøget, Christiania, Nyhavn, Kongens Nytorv and Kastrup Airport; 'Take extra care in Christiania and Nørrebro, particularly late at night'; 'Cyclists often have the right of way. Always check cycle lanes before turning right.' Re-cited. EN+AR.

entries.new: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Djibouti.

entries.old: The eVisa application asks for a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation, and airlines check tickets before boarding flights to Djibouti.
entries.new: The eVisa application asks for a flight reservation (or other means of transport), an accommodation address (hotel or host) and an invitation letter.

It names a flight reservation, not a return or onward ticket, and nothing official says airlines check tickets.

entries.old: Djibouti City and the main tourist sites are generally safe, with petty theft the main concern. Stay well away from the Eritrean border area and be cautious in remote regions. Carry ID, expect checkpoints, and check current advisories for the wider region before travel.
entries.new: The UK advises against all travel to the Djibouti–Eritrea border. Elsewhere the main risk is petty crime, so keep valuables, particularly cameras and passports, out of sight, and avoid travelling outside city centres after dark.
entries.note: FCDO: "FCDO advises against all travel to the Djibouti-Eritrea border"; "There is a risk of petty crime ... keeping valuables, particularly cameras and passports, out of sight"; "avoid travelling outside city centres after dark". Carrying ID and checkpoints are not on the FCDO pages.

entries.old: Cash or bearer instruments worth XCD 10,000 or more (roughly USD 3,700) must be declared to customs on arrival and departure.
entries.new: Cash or travellers' cheques worth XCD 10,000 or more (roughly USD 3,700) must be declared to customs when you bring them in; you receive a certified declaration showing you brought the money with you.
entries.note: FCDO: "Declare cash or travellers cheques if the value is 10,000 East Caribbean dollars or more. You will get a certified declaration to show you brought it in with you." The source states the duty on entry only; "and departure" withdrawn.

entries.old: For tourists, the Dominican Republic requires your passport to be valid for the duration of your stay. There is no formal 6-month rule, though airlines sometimes apply stricter checks of their own.
entries.new: For tourists, the Dominican Republic requires your passport to be valid for the duration of your stay. There is no formal 6-month rule, though airlines sometimes apply stricter checks of their own. The UK government says this rule applies up to 31 December 2026 and may change after that date.
entries.note: FCDO: "Up until 31 December 2026, British passport holders can enter and leave ... as long as their passport remains valid for the duration of their visit. Rules may change after this date." Time limit added.

entries.old: Resort areas such as Punta Cana are heavily policed (CESTUR tourist police) and generally safe; petty theft, bag-snatching from motorbikes and occasional armed robbery are risks in cities, especially after dark. Keep valuables out of sight, use trusted transport, and stick to well-lit areas at night.
entries.new: The UK government describes the crime rate as high, from bag-snatching and pickpocketing to violent crime and carjacking. Thieves on motorcycles snatch bags from pedestrians and reach into cars stopped at red lights, and assaults on foreigners have occurred at beach resorts. Keep valuables out of sight, use trusted transport, and avoid remote areas after dark.
entries.note: FCDO: "The crime rate in the Dominican Republic is high. Incidents range from opportunistic bag-snatching and pickpocketing to violent crime and carjacking." The page says nothing of CESTUR or of resort areas being generally safe; it reports assaults "including at beach resorts". Unsourced reassurance withdrawn.

entries.old: Ecuador's security situation deteriorated sharply from 2023, with gang violence, armed robbery, express kidnappings and repeated states of emergency. The UK advises against all but essential travel to the coastal provinces of Esmeraldas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Guayas (including Guayaquil, except airside transit at its airport), El Oro, Los Ríos and Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, and to within 20 km of the Colombian border. A 60-day state of emergency declared on 15 September 2026 covers eight provinces, including Pichincha (Quito), with night curfews in four. The highlands outside those areas and the Galápagos are not covered by the advice against travel, but check current advice before you go.
entries.new: Ecuador's security situation deteriorated sharply from 2023, with gang violence, armed robbery, express kidnappings and repeated states of emergency. The UK advises against all but essential travel to the coastal provinces of Esmeraldas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Guayas (including Guayaquil, except airside transit at its airport), El Oro, Los Ríos and Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas, and to within 20 km of the Colombian border. A 60-day state of emergency declared on 15 September 2026 covers eight provinces, including Pichincha (Quito), with midnight-to-5am curfews in four of them (El Oro, Guayas, Los Ríos and Manabí) from 17 to 30 September. The highlands outside those areas and the Galápagos are not covered by the advice against travel, but check current advice before you go.
entries.note: FCDO (updated 2 October 2026): the state of emergency "includes curfew hours (from 12am to 5am) for the provinces of El Oro, Guayas, Los Rios and Manabi, from 17 to 30 September." The curfews were time-limited and have ended; the text no longer implies they are ongoing.

entries.old: Main tourist areas (Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, the Nile Valley and Red Sea resorts) are heavily policed and generally safe for visitors, but avoid the North Sinai governorate and the Western Desert near the Libyan border, and expect security checkpoints when traveling between cities.
entries.new: The UK advises against all travel to North Sinai and to within 20 km of the Libyan border, and against all but essential travel to most of the Western Desert, northern South Sinai beyond the St Catherine–Nuweiba road, Ismailiyah east of the Suez Canal and the Hala'ib Triangle. Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, the Nile Valley and the Red Sea coast lie outside these areas. Expect security checkpoints when traveling between cities.
