entries.old: Apply at least 60 days before travel.
entries.new: A visa is required. Equatorial Guinea cancelled visa-free travel for US passport holders on 24 April 2023, and its Embassy in Washington states that all visitors with a foreign passport must present a valid visa. An older government information page still describes the exemption; we follow the Embassy, since travelling without a visa risks being refused boarding or entry. The US Embassy in Malabo says to apply at least 60 days before travel, and the Embassy of Equatorial Guinea says a visa must be used within 60 days of issuance, so time the application with both in mind.
entries.note: US Embassy Malabo: 'At least 60 days before travel to EG, apply for a visa at the nearest EG Embassy or consulate' — the advice is real, not a misreading. Added the Equatoguinean Embassy's 'Visas must be used within 60 days of issuance', which bounds it from the other side. Same in the tip and FAQ.

entries.old: Broadly yes in terms of crime, which is low by regional standards. The friction points are bureaucratic: frequent police checkpoints, strict photography rules and document checks. Keep your papers on you, avoid photographing anything official, and travel patiently.
entries.new: Take care. The UK government says crime ranges from petty theft and mugging to carjacking and armed robbery, with greater risk after dark in remote parts of Malabo and Bata. Police and military roadblocks are common, with regular reports of requests for bribes, and photographing government or military buildings or airports is illegal. Keep your papers on you and travel patiently.
entries.note: FCDO: 'Crimes range from petty theft and mugging to carjacking and armed robbery, risks can be greater in remote areas of towns, particularly after dark including around Malabo and Bata'; 'regular reports of police and uniformed security forces at roadblocks asking for bribes'. 'Crime ... low by regional standards' had no source.

entries.old: Violent crime is comparatively rare, but travelers face frequent police checkpoints, document checks and occasional petty extortion; photography rules are strictly enforced. Carry certified copies of your passport and visa at all times.
entries.new: Crime ranges from petty theft and mugging to carjacking and armed robbery, with greater risk after dark in remote parts of Malabo and Bata. Always carry your passport or residence permit, or copies.

entries.old: Day-to-day street crime in Asmara is low, but Eritrea is a tightly controlled state where several governments advise heightened caution or against non-essential travel: movement outside the capital requires permits, border areas with Ethiopia and Djibouti are militarised with landmine risks, communications are restricted and consular assistance is extremely limited.

The UK advises against all travel within 25 km of Eritrea's land borders, where there are landmines; foreign nationals need a permit to travel outside the Asmara region, and consular assistance is severely limited.
entries.note: FCDO: 'Though Asmara is a relatively safe city, there is a risk of street crime, especially at night'; 'FCDO advises against all travel to within 25km of all of Eritrea's land borders'; permits needed outside Zoba Maekel; landmines near borders; consular support severely limited. 'Several governments advise heightened caution', 'militarised' Ethiopia/Djibouti borders and 'communications are restricted' are not on the cited page.

entries.old: Street crime in Asmara is rare, but the wider picture demands caution: several governments advise against non-essential travel, border zones are militarised with landmine risks, movement is controlled by permits, communications are restricted and consular help is extremely limited. entries.new: The UK advises against all travel to the Tigray, Amhara and Gambela regions, to parts of Afar (within 20km of the Eritrean border and 50km of the Tigray boundary), Oromia, Somali and Benishangul-Gumuz, and to most land border areas, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz and to further parts of Oromia and Somali. All civilian flights to and from Tigray were suspended on 22 September 2026. Conflict and kidnapping are reported in parts of Amhara, Oromia and Somali, and mugging is on the rise in Addis Ababa. Check current government travel advice before planning any trip outside the capital.
entries.note: FCDO (updated 1 October 2026): "FCDO advises against all travel to: ... the Metekel zone, the Maokomo special zone" and "against all but essential travel to the rest of Benishangul-Gumuz region"; all-but-essential areas also listed in Oromia (East Shewa, North Shewa, Guji zones) and Somali (Siti, Nogob, Jarar, Shabelle...); "All civilian flights to and from Tigray region were suspended on 22 September 2026."

entries.old: Visitors must hold a confirmed onward or return ticket and be able to name where they are staying — both are conditions of the visitor permit granted on arrival, and airlines check the ticket before boarding.
entries.new: At border control visitors must show an onward or return ticket and a valid visa for the next country they are travelling to. Fiji's immigration ministry likewise asks for an onward ticket for the next destination after Fiji.
entries.note: FCDO: 'At Fiji border control, you must also show: an onward or return ticket; a valid visa for the next country you're travelling to'. Ministry's Visit Fiji page (Wayback 20260518): 'Proof of approved visa and onward ticket for the next country of destination after Fiji is needed.' The unsourced 'be able to name where they are staying' is removed.

entries.old: Issued mainly alongside residence-permit decisions for workers, students, researchers and their families. Most stays over 90 days are handled as residence permits through the Finnish Immigration Service (Migri). Confirm current conditions with the Finnish mission.
entries.new: €95 when applied for through the electronic e-service; €120 on a paper application. Issued mainly alongside residence-permit decisions for workers, students, researchers and their families. Most stays over 90 days are handled as residence permits through the Finnish Immigration Service (Migri). Confirm current conditions with the Finnish mission.
entries.note: um.fi service fees: 'D visa, paper application 120' and 'D visa, electronic application, e-service 95'. The €95 figure is the e-service price; the paper price was missing.

entries.old: Finland consistently ranks among the safest countries in the world, with very low crime. The main risks are environmental: severe winter cold in Lapland and slippery pavements in the cities.
entries.new: Pickpockets may target tourists in crowded areas during the tourist season. Parts of Finland lie inside the Arctic Circle, where some areas are very remote and emergency medical help and search and rescue are limited.
entries.note: FCDO Finland: 'Pickpockets may target tourists in the tourist season in crowded areas' and 'Parts of Finland are in the Arctic Circle, including some very remote areas of land. Emergency medical assistance and search and rescue are limited in these areas.' It says nothing of world safety rankings, Lapland cold or slippery pavements. Level very-safe unchanged.

entries.old: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Gabon, with at least one blank page for the entry stamp or visa.
entries.new: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Gabon.
entries.note: FCDO: 'Your passport must have an expiry date that is at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Gabon.' The blank-page clause is not on the page; withdrawn.

entries.old: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from all travelers aged 1 year and over and is routinely checked on arrival. Keep the yellow card with your passport.
entries.new: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter Gabon. Keep the yellow card with your passport.
entries.note: FCDO: 'To enter Gabon, you must have a certificate to prove you've had a yellow fever vaccination.' The age threshold and 'routinely checked on arrival' are not on the cited page; withdrawn.

entries.old: No. Gabon announced visa exemptions for several Western countries in late 2023, but they no longer cover EU, UK, Canadian or US citizens: Spain's foreign ministry says EU citizens are no longer exempt, France and the Netherlands tell their citizens to get a visa through the DGDI, and the UK and Canada list a visa as required. The US State Department reports that Gabon announced on 18 December 2025 that it would suspend visa issuance to US citizens, in reciprocity for US restrictions that took effect on 1 January 2026.
entries.new: No. Gabon announced visa exemptions for several Western countries in late 2023, but they no longer cover EU, Norwegian, UK, Canadian or US citizens: Spain's foreign ministry says EU citizens are no longer exempt, France and the Netherlands tell their citizens to get a visa through the DGDI, Norway says Norwegians need a visa, and the UK and Canada list a visa as required. No official source confirms an exemption for Swiss, Icelandic or Liechtenstein citizens either. The US State Department reports that Gabon announced on 18 December 2025 that it would suspend visa issuance to US citizens, in reciprocity for US restrictions that took effect on 1 January 2026.
entries.note: Adds Norway (visa required) and the withdrawn CH/IS/LI exemption.

entries.old: Yes. Gabon requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate from all travelers aged 1 year and over, regardless of where you are arriving from, and it is checked on arrival.
entries.new: Yes. You must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Gabon, whatever country you are arriving from.
entries.note: Age threshold and 'checked on arrival' are not stated by the cited source; withdrawn.

entries.old: Gabon is calmer than much of the region, but petty crime occurs in Libreville and Port-Gentil, and the political situation has been in transition since 2023. Avoid demonstrations and keep documents on you.
entries.new: Robbery, armed attacks and rape have occurred in Gabon, including assaults on taxi passengers, so avoid remote areas and isolated beaches after dark. Since the August 2023 military takeover the authorities may scrutinise tourists closely, and some have been held and questioned. Avoid protests and rallies and carry your documents.
entries.note: FCDO: 'There have been incidents of robbery, armed attacks and rape in Gabon'; 'reports of violent assaults and robberies on taxi passengers'; after the August 2023 coup 'some tourists being held and questioned ... the authorities may treat tourists with heightened scrutiny'. 'Petty crime' understated it; 'calmer than much of the region' is not on the page. Level unchanged (no advise-against).

entries.old: ECOWAS citizens enter freely under the Community's free-movement protocol — up to 90 days with a valid passport or ECOWAS travel document.
entries.new: Burkina Faso left ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, but the ECOWAS Commission has announced that its citizens continue to enjoy, until further notice, movement, residence and establishment without a visa under the Community’s protocols; The Gambia’s Immigration Department says citizens of Mauritania, Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso “will enjoy privileges as accorded”. Up to 90 days with a valid passport or ECOWAS travel document.
entries.note: Brief: AES rows must rest on an official statement of what now applies. ECOWAS Commission, 30 Jan 2025: "the citizens of these states continue to enjoy, until further notice, the right of movement, residence and establishment without visas, in accordance with the regional organization’s protocols"; GID /visa/ (live) no longer lists BF/ML/NE among "ECOWAS Member States Allows Free Entry" and says "Citizens of The Islamic Republic of Mauritania, Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso will enjoy privileges as accorded." Requirement (freedom-of-movement, 90 days) unchanged. Arabic overlay updated. Row source is the GID visa page (which states the "privileges as accorded" line); the ECOWAS Commission statement (https://www.ecowas.int/burkina-faso-mali-and-nigers-withdrawal-from-ecowas-is-now-a-reality/) is quoted in the note but cannot be cited until www.ecowas.int is registered in official-hosts.json.

entries.old: 28 (extendable 56)
entries.note: Row had no source. Ireland DFA: "Irish citizens can enter The Gambia without a visa for up to 90 days but must provide: proof of sufficient funds, documents showing proof of purpose of trip, proof of onward/return ticket within 90 days of arrival, proof of regular residence in Ireland." GID does not name Ireland. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: The Gambia admits ECOWAS citizens, most Commonwealth nationals and much of northern Europe visa-free — visitors are stamped in for 28 days, which can be extended twice by 28 days in Banjul (ECOWAS citizens may stay up to 90 days) — while US, French and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.
entries.new: The Gambia admits ECOWAS citizens, the UK, Canada, Australia and much of northern Europe visa-free — British visitors are stamped in for 28 days, which can be extended twice by 28 days in Banjul (ECOWAS citizens may stay up to 90 days) — while citizens of much of the Caribbean, the Pacific, East and Southern Africa and South-East Asia need an entry clearance that a host in The Gambia obtains in advance from the Immigration Department, and US, French and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.
entries.note: "most Commonwealth nationals ... visa-free" no longer true: GID lists most Commonwealth countries under "Need Only Clearance" or "Need Both Visa And Clearance". The 28-day stamp is FCDO's statement for British visitors. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: Citizens of ECOWAS states, most Commonwealth countries and much of northern and western Europe — including the UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Scandinavia — enter visa-free; visitors are stamped in for 28 days, ECOWAS citizens for up to 90. US, French, Portuguese and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.
entries.new: Citizens of ECOWAS states and of much of northern and western Europe — including the UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and Scandinavia — enter visa-free, as do Canadians and Australians; British visitors are stamped in for 28 days, while Irish citizens may stay up to 90 days and ECOWAS citizens up to 90. Citizens of much of the Caribbean, the Pacific, East and Southern Africa and South-East Asia need no visa but an entry clearance, which a host in The Gambia obtains in advance from the Immigration Department. US, French, Portuguese and various other passport holders need a visa from a Gambian embassy before travel.
entries.note: Follows the rows: GID clearance-only list; Ireland DFA "up to 90 days"; FCDO 28-day stamp is for British visitors; "most Commonwealth countries" dropped. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: Border officers stamp visitors in for 28 days whatever their visa status; ECOWAS citizens can stay up to 90 days under the Community's free-movement protocol. Stays can be extended twice, by 28 days each time, at the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area. Apply before your stamp expires.
entries.new: The UK government says British visitors are stamped in for 28 days on arrival, and Ireland says Irish citizens can stay up to 90 days; ECOWAS citizens can stay up to 90 days under the Community's free-movement protocol. Stays can be extended twice, by 28 days each time, at the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area. Apply before your stamp expires.
entries.note: FCDO: "You'll get a stamp in your passport that allows you to stay for 28 days" is written for British citizens; Ireland DFA: "Irish citizens can enter The Gambia without a visa for up to 90 days". "whatever their visa status" was not stated. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: Unless you are an ECOWAS citizen (up to 90 days), border officers stamp you in for 28 days whatever your visa status — for longer stays, extend at the Immigration Department in Banjul before the stamp expires.
entries.new: Unless you are an ECOWAS citizen (up to 90 days), expect a 28-day entry stamp — the period the UK government gives for British visitors (Ireland says Irish citizens may stay up to 90 days). For longer stays, extend at the Immigration Department in Banjul before the stamp expires.
entries.note: "whatever your visa status" not stated; FCDO 28 days is for British visitors, Ireland DFA says 90 for Irish citizens. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 9 months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — commonly checked for arrivals overland or via mainland West Africa.
entries.new: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 9 months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.
entries.note: FCDO states only "you must have a certificate ... if you're coming from a country listed as a transmission risk" — no age. WHO Annex 1: "Gambia Yes Yes5 (≥ 9 months)", so the 9-month figure is now cited to WHO. "commonly checked for arrivals overland or via mainland West Africa" is stated by no source and was removed. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: 1–3 business days
entries.new: null (not published)
entries.note: FCDO: "You can get 2 extensions of 28 days from the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area." — confirms 28 + 28, but states no processing time; GID publishes none either. Withdrawn.

entries.old: The Gambia is one of West Africa's calmer destinations and most visits are trouble-free. Petty theft and persistent hustling by "bumsters" on tourist beaches are the main annoyances; use registered taxis at night.
entries.new: The UK government has no warning against travel to The Gambia. Petty theft is a problem in cities and tourist areas, especially at night on isolated beaches, in markets and at crowded events; persistent "bumsters" approach tourists on the beaches; and security checkpoints operate on all major routes.
entries.note: FCDO (read 2026-10-03 via content API): no advice against travel; "Petty theft is a problem in cities and tourist areas ... especially at night, such as: isolated beaches, markets, crowded events"; "Be cautious of young men locally known as 'bumsters'"; "Security checkpoints ... are common on all major routes". "one of West Africa's calmer destinations", "most visits are trouble-free" and "use registered taxis at night" are not stated and were removed. Arabic overlay updated.

entries.old: 1–5 business days
entries.new: null (at least 5 working days, no upper bound published)
entries.note: e-Visa FAQ: "It takes not less then 5 working days to make a decision on a visa application." The old 1–5 range had the minimum as its maximum. Fee "20 USD + 2% service fee" confirmed.

entries.old: Holders of a GCC residence permit (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain or Oman) can enter Georgia visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period — since 16 May 2025 the permit must be valid for at least 12 more months for citizens of 17 listed countries.

entries.old: Guyana has a high rate of violent and armed crime, concentrated in Georgetown — particularly Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay and the seawall after dark. Use pre-booked taxis rather than minibuses at night, keep phones and jewellery out of sight, and treat interior travel as remote wilderness travel with no quick rescue.
entries.new: Crime levels are significant and police capacity is low. Muggings and attacks, sometimes with knives or firearms, happen in daylight but more often at night and can target tourists who show signs of wealth; reported hotspots in Georgetown include Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay, Albouystown and the Botanical Gardens. Gangs have followed cars from Cheddi Jagan International Airport, so drive with doors locked and use a taxi booked by your hotel or a licensed operator.
entries.note: The seawall and 'remote wilderness... no quick rescue' are on no FCDO page; the cited front page has no safety detail. FCDO safety page: 'Crime levels are significant, and police capacity is low'; 'Attacks and muggings have occurred in broad daylight but are more common at night... knives or firearms'; Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay and Albouystown; 'assaulted in Georgetown's Botanical Gardens'; 'gangs following cars from Cheddi Jagan International Airport'. Re-cited. EN+AR.

entries.old: It depends on your passport. CARICOM nationals travel freely and are normally admitted for six months. entries.old: Iceland has one of the lowest crime rates in the world. The real risks are natural: rapidly changing weather, wind-blown car doors, unstable volcanic areas and dangerous surf at beaches like Reynisfjara — follow safetravel.is guidance.
entries.new: Crime levels are low, though petty theft and antisocial behaviour occur, particularly around bars in downtown Reykjavík. The bigger risks are natural: weather that changes quickly and makes driving hard, strong winds that can damage rental cars, and the volcanic eruptions on the Reykjanes peninsula since December 2023 — follow the authorities' latest advice.
entries.note: FCDO Iceland 'Safety and security': 'Crime levels are low but petty theft and antisocial behaviour can occur, particularly around bars in downtown Reykjavík'; it names quickly changing weather, wind damage to rental cars and the Reykjanes eruptions since December 2023. entries.old: Most visits are trouble-free, but petty crime, traffic and scams around tourist sites warrant increased caution. Women travelers should take particular care, especially at night. Avoid border areas with Pakistan and parts of the northeast.
entries.new: Most visits are trouble-free, but petty crime, traffic and scams around tourist sites warrant increased caution. Women travelers should take particular care, especially at night. The UK advises against all travel within 10 km of the Pakistan border and to Jammu and Kashmir (except travel by air to and within the city of Jammu), and against all but essential travel to Manipur.
entries.note: FCDO: all travel within 10km of the India-Pakistan border; all travel to the UT of Jammu and Kashmir except by air to and within Jammu; all but essential travel to Manipur. 'Parts of the northeast' was vaguer than the source and J&K was missing.

entries.field: Visa on arrival at land borders
entries.old: Visa on arrival is issued only at major international airports (Tehran IKA, Shiraz, Isfahan, Mashhad and others) — never at land borders. Arriving overland, you need the eVisa approval first.
entries.new: Iran's MFA describes visa on arrival only at its international airports (such as Tehran IKA); it says nothing about land borders, so if you arrive overland get the eVisa approval first.
entries.note: The MFA VOA page (read 2026-10-03) says only 'Apply for all Iranian International Airports' and that fees are paid 'through banking terminals at airport'; it does not say VOA is never issued at land borders. Silence is not a statement: the 'never' claim was removed from the tip and 148 row notes.

entries.old: Turkish citizens are not among the 44 nationalities that Iraq's e-Visa portal lets apply directly online, and Iraq does not state a visa on arrival for them. Apply in advance at an Iraqi embassy or consulate. The Kurdistan Region runs a separate entry regime whose visas are valid there only.
entries.new: Türkiye's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says Turkish ordinary-passport holders under 15 or over 50 are exempt from a visa for 30 days; those aged 15 to 50 need a visa. Turkey is not among the 44 nationalities that Iraq's e-Visa portal lets apply directly online, so apply in advance at an Iraqi embassy or consulate. The Kurdistan Region runs a separate entry regime whose visas are valid there only.
entries.note: Settles the open TR question. Turkish MFA table: 'Irak: 15 yaşından küçük ve 50 yaşından büyük umuma mahsus pasaport hamilleri 30 gün süreyle vizeden muaftır. 15-50 yaş arasındaki umuma mahsus pasaport hamilleri vizeye tabidir.' Requirement stays embassy-visa (it applies to the 15–50 majority); the age exemption is now stated in the note. Row source moved from the e-Visa list (silent on Turks) to the Turkish MFA statement.

entries.new: null
entries.note: No official source states the 30-day stay or the visa exemption for Iranians: mofa.gov.iq does not, Iraq's e-Visa portal nationality search returns no countries (api empty), and the Iranian MFA host refused. Guessed stay withdrawn; note now says plainly the exemption is unconfirmed. Requirement left as it was pending an official statement.

entries.old: Yes. Iraq no longer issues visit visas on arrival: the UK, Canadian and Australian governments all say you must get a visa before you travel, usually the e-Visa on Iraq's official portal (evisa.iq). The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and the validity as 60 days; Iraq's portal says 30 days, so plan on 30. Apply at least 24 hours before departure — airlines check for the visa before boarding. Nationalities not eligible for the e-Visa apply at an Iraqi embassy. The exception is Iran: under a bilateral agreement, Iranian citizens arriving by air can enter without a visa.
entries.new: Yes. Iraq no longer issues visit visas on arrival: the UK, Canadian and Australian governments all say you must get a visa before you travel, usually the e-Visa on Iraq's official portal (evisa.iq). The FCDO gives the fee as USD 160 and the validity as 60 days; Iraq's portal says 30 days, so plan on 30. Apply at least 24 hours before departure — airlines check for the visa before boarding. Nationalities not eligible for the e-Visa apply at an Iraqi embassy. Turkey's foreign ministry says Turkish citizens under 15 or over 50 are visa-exempt for 30 days. Iranian citizens arriving by air are widely reported to enter without a visa, but no official source we could read confirms it.
entries.note: Follows the TR and IR row changes.

entries.old: 15–40 business-days
entries.new: 0–56 calendar-days (within approximately 8 weeks)
entries.note: How-to-apply page: 'applicants can expect a decision within approximately 8 weeks from the date their application was received'. The 15-business-day minimum was not stated.

entries.old: Not a formal requirement, but immigration officers at the border may ask non-EEA visitors about return or onward travel, accommodation and funds before granting permission to enter.
entries.new: Not among the documents the Irish Immigration Service says you must present (passport, visa if needed, boarding card). It lists a travel itinerary, proof of sufficient funds, proof of health insurance and accommodation details among other useful documents an officer may ask about.
entries.note: Border page: 'At a minimum, this includes: Your passport; Visa (if necessary); Boarding card. Other useful documents may include: A travel itinerary; Proof of sufficient funds; Proof of health insurance ...; Details of your accommodation'. It does not mention a return or onward ticket; text aligned.

entries.old: Cash and negotiable instruments worth ILS 50,000 or more (about USD 13,000) must be declared on arrival and departure.
entries.new: Cash and other means of payment (cheques, bearer securities, negotiable instruments, payment cards) worth ILS 50,000 or more must be declared on entry and exit at any border crossing. The threshold is ILS 12,000 at the Nizana, Jordan River and Yitzhak Rabin land crossings, and JOD 2,000 at the Allenby crossing.
entries.note: Live page answers 403 (Cloudflare) to curl and headless Chrome; read from Wayback 20250616092149: 'ILS 50,000 or more and coming through any border crossing; ILS 12,000 or more and crossing through: Nizana crossing, The Jordan River crossing, Yitzhak Rabin crossing; Dinar 2,000 or more and crossing through Allenby crossing'. Not a conflict: one source, different crossings; both written in. The USD conversion was dropped.

entries.old: 5-30 business days
entries.new: null (not stated)
entries.note: The MFA consular tariff confirms 'B/2-Visitor Visa' USD 32 / EUR 28 but states no processing time; withdrawn.

entries.old: Italy is a very safe destination. The main risks for visitors are pickpocketing on public transport in Rome, Milan and Naples, and around crowded sights and train stations.
entries.new: Crime levels are generally low, but bag-snatching and pickpocketing are more common in city centres and at major tourist attractions.
entries.note: FCDO Italy 'Safety and security' (updated 2 Oct 2026): 'Crime levels are generally low but there are higher levels of petty crime, particularly bag-snatching and pickpocketing, in city centres and at major tourist attractions.' The previous text named Rome, Milan and Naples and public transport, which the FCDO does not; citation moved to the page that states it.

entries.old: Jamaica is visa-free for citizens of the US (for up to six months), Canada, the UK, most of the EU and most Commonwealth countries, though the period is 90 days for some passports and 30 for others, including France, Spain and most of Latin America. CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months, and a few nationalities can buy a visa at the port of entry. Whatever your nationality, every arriving passenger must complete Jamaica's free online immigration and customs (C5) form before traveling.
entries.new: Jamaica is visa-free for citizens of the US (for up to six months), Canada, the UK, most of the EU and most Commonwealth countries, though the period is 90 days for some passports and 30 for others, including France, Spain and most of Latin America. CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months, and a few nationalities can buy a visa at the port of entry. Whatever your nationality, every arriving passenger must present Jamaica's free immigration and customs (C5) form, completed online before travel where possible or on paper.
entries.note: PICA accepts the C5 online or on paper.

entries.old: The C5 is Jamaica's combined immigration and customs declaration, completed online at enterjamaica.gov.jm before you travel. It is mandatory for every arriving passenger regardless of nationality, it is free, and you should carry the QR code or a printout. Most people fill it in within 72 hours of their flight.
entries.new: The C5 is Jamaica's combined immigration and customs declaration. It is mandatory for every arriving passenger regardless of nationality, and it is free. PICA accepts it either online at enterjamaica.gov.jm or as a signed paper form; the UK government advises completing it online before you arrive where possible.
entries.note: PICA: "either online or a physical form". The 72-hour habit and the QR-code requirement are stated by no official source and were withdrawn.

entries.old: Jamaica has one of the highest homicide rates in the Americas, but the violence is heavily concentrated in specific inner-city districts of Kingston, Spanish Town and Montego Bay that visitors have no reason to enter. entries.old: Malaysia grants visa-free entry to most nationalities — 90 days for US, UK, EU and many other passports, 30 days for most ASEAN neighbors, Chinese citizens (visa-free since 1 September 2026) and Indian citizens (exemption extended through 2026), and requires almost all foreign arrivals to submit the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online within 3 days before travel.
entries.new: Malaysia grants visa-free entry to most nationalities — up to a month for ASEAN neighbors except Myanmar, 30 days for Chinese citizens (visa-free since 1 September 2026) and Indian citizens (exemption extended through 2026), and requires almost all foreign arrivals to submit the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online within 3 days before travel.
entries.note: 90-day figure for US/UK/EU withdrawn (only FCDO states 90 for British visitors); ASEAN rule restated as the IMI page gives it. EN+AR.

entries.old: No. US passport holders enter Malaysia visa-free for up to 90 days. The only mandatory step is the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), submitted online within 3 days before arrival.
entries.new: No. US passport holders enter Malaysia without a visa; Malaysia's Immigration Department does not publish how long US citizens may stay. The only mandatory step is the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), submitted online within 3 days before arrival.
entries.note: 90 days for US citizens is stated by no official source read. EN+AR.

entries.old: Malaysia is generally safe for visitors; petty theft such as bag-snatching occurs in cities. Western governments advise extra caution in the eastern coastal areas of Sabah due to kidnapping risk.
entries.new: Bag-snatching is common in major cities, often by thieves on motorbikes, and credit card and ATM fraud is widespread. The UK government advises against all but essential travel to the islands and dive sites off eastern Sabah, from Sandakan to Tawau, because of the threat of kidnapping; this does not apply to the Sabah mainland.
entries.note: FCDO: 'FCDO advises against all but essential travel to all islands and dive sites off the coast of eastern Sabah from Sandakan to Tawau, including Lankayan Island, due to the threat of kidnapping. This does not apply to the mainland of Sabah.' The old 'eastern coastal areas of Sabah' overstated the area. Safety page: 'Bag-snatching is common, particularly in major cities. Thieves on motorbikes can target tourists'; 'Credit card and ATM fraud is widespread.' EN+AR.

entries.old: Yes. The free 30-day visa on arrival can be extended in-country by applying through Maldives Immigration (via the Imuga portal) before your first 30 days expire, with proof of accommodation and funds; Immigration expects to decide applications within 48 hours. It does not publish the maximum length of an extension. A fee applies.
entries.new: Yes. The free 30-day visa on arrival can be extended in-country by applying through the IMUGA portal before your first 30 days expire. Your passport and accommodation details are filled in automatically (you can update your hotel if you have moved) and you upload a recent photo; Immigration expects to decide applications within 48 hours. It does not publish the maximum length of an extension or the fee.
entries.note: Repetition: 'A fee applies' and 'with proof of accommodation and funds' are not stated in the 24 April 2026 notice; replaced with what it does say.

entries.old: The Maldives is a safe destination, especially on resort islands. Petty theft can occur in Malé and on local islands; the biggest real risks are strong ocean currents and snorkelling or diving incidents — follow local guidance.
entries.new: Crime is low on the resort islands, but petty theft happens — do not leave things unattended on the beach or in unlocked rooms. Outside the resorts there is gang-related violence, including knife crime, mainly in Malé and Hulhumalé; avoid empty roads on foot after dark. Strong tidal currents cause drownings, so swim only in supervised or designated areas.
entries.note: FCDO 'Safety and security': 'Crime levels are low in the exclusive resort islands, but petty crime does happen... Outside the resorts, there are incidents of gang-related violence including knife crime, mainly in Malé and in Hulhumalé.' The previous text called it 'a safe destination' with only petty theft in Malé, omitting the gang and knife-crime warning.

entries.old: The west-coast corridor (Nouakchott, Nouadhibou, Banc d'Arguin) and the Adrar see travelers routinely, but areas near the Mali border and the remote east and north are under do-not-travel advisories due to terrorism risk. Petty crime is moderate; the bigger constraints are distance, heat and thin infrastructure.
entries.new: The west-coast corridor (Nouakchott, Nouadhibou, Banc d'Arguin) and the western Adrar around Atar, Chinguetti and Ouadane see travelers routinely. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to the east and to within 25 km of the Mali border because of terrorism risk, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the interior, including the southern provinces. Petty crime is moderate; the bigger constraints are distance, heat and thin infrastructure.
entries.note: FCDO: "advises against all travel to areas east of a line drawn between ... Kankossa, Akhreijit, Ghallaouia, Zouerat, Fderîck"; "all travel to areas within 25km of the Malian border"; "all but essential travel to the rest of the province of Tiris Zemmour, Assaba, Hodh el Gharbi, Gorgol and Guidimaka, and areas of Adrar and Tagant", excluding "the areas west of a line running between Choum, Ouadane" and "the town of Ouadane". The old text implied the whole Adrar was routine and omitted the all-but-essential advisory.

entries.old: Mauritius is one of Africa's safest destinations, with little serious crime. Petty theft around beaches and tourist areas is the main risk — do not leave valuables unattended — and swimmers should stay inside the lagoons, away from reef currents.
entries.new: Most crime is non-violent, such as burglaries from tourist villas and theft of unattended bags, but petty crime is common in tourist areas such as Port Louis, Grand Baie and Flic en Flac, and there have been some reports of sexual assaults on tourists. Avoid walking alone at night on beaches or in poorly lit areas.

'One of Africa's safest destinations' and the lagoon/reef-current advice are not on the cited page.

entries.old: Visa-free visitors are normally admitted for up to 90 days (60 days for British, Chinese and Russian citizens and most visa-on-arrival nationalities, two weeks for a few). The immigration officer sets the length of each stay on arrival. Tourist stays can be extended by the Passport and Immigration Office in Port Louis up to a maximum of 180 days in a calendar year, with proof of funds and accommodation.
entries.new: EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Mauritius visa waiver agreement. British, Canadian, Chinese and Russian citizens are admitted for up to 60 days, as are most visa-on-arrival nationalities (two weeks for a few). For other visa-free nationalities no maximum is published: the immigration officer sets the length of each stay on arrival. Tourist stays can be extended by the Passport and Immigration Office in Port Louis, with proof of funds and accommodation.
entries.note: Follows the row corrections; the '180 days in a calendar year' extension cap is stated on no PIO page and was dropped.

entries.old: Cash and monetary instruments over 10,000 USD (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure; failing to declare can mean seizure and fines.
entries.new: Anyone entering or leaving Mexico with more than USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) in cash, cheques or other monetary documents must declare it to customs. Carrying the money is not an offence; failing to declare it is fined 20–40% of the amount above USD 10,000, and an undeclared amount over USD 30,000 can mean 3 months to 6 years in prison and forfeiture of the excess.
entries.note: ANAM: "Si no lo declaras, serás acreedor a una multa del 20% al 40% sobre la cantidad que exceda a los 10 mil dólares. Si la cantidad que no declaraste es mayor a 30 mil Dólares americanos, serás sancionado con una pena de 3 meses a 6 años de prisión y el excedente pasará a ser propiedad del Fisco Federal". Vague "seizure and fines" replaced with the stated penalties.

entries.old: Safety varies dramatically by state: major tourist areas are heavily policed and generally trouble-free, while several states carry do-not-travel advisories due to organized crime. Check the state-by-state US advisory for your exact route and avoid intercity road travel at night.
entries.new: Safety varies sharply by state. The UK government advises against all but essential travel to all or parts of several states, including Zacatecas, Michoacán, Sinaloa, Tamaulipas, Chihuahua and parts of Baja California and Guanajuato, because of organised-crime violence. Risks are lower in tourist areas, though sexual offences have been reported there too. Check the advice for every state on your route and avoid travelling in higher-risk areas at night.
entries.note: FCDO lists states and areas where it "advises against all but essential travel" and says "While risks are lower in tourist areas" and "Sexual offences have been reported in tourist areas". The cited UK page says nothing of tourist areas being "heavily policed and generally trouble-free" nor of a US state-by-state advisory; text aligned with the cited source.

entries.old: Mexico is not one uniform risk level. A handful of states are under do-not-travel advisories while the main tourist corridors are fine. Check advice for each state on your itinerary, not just the country page.

entries.old: A free 30-day visitor entry permit is issued on arrival to citizens of essentially every country. Bring a passport valid at least 120 days beyond your date of entry and a confirmed onward ticket. Extensions are granted by the FSM Division of Immigration.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: Almost certainly not. Citizens of essentially every country are admitted without a visa and receive a free 30-day entry permit on arrival, provided they hold a passport valid well beyond the stay and an onward ticket. US citizens need no visa under the Compact of Free Association, and their entry permit can cover the whole visit, up to one year.
entries.new: Almost certainly not. Citizens of essentially every country need neither a visa nor a permit for visits of 30 days or less, provided they hold a passport valid at least 120 days beyond the date of entry and a return or onward ticket; stays over 30 days need an entry permit. US citizens need no visa under the Compact of Free Association, and their entry permit can cover the whole visit, up to one year.

entries.old: Morocco is generally safe for visitors with a strong tourist-police presence in the main cities. The most common problems are pickpocketing, aggressive touts and "faux guides" in the medinas of Marrakech and Fes — be polite but firm, and agree taxi and guide prices in advance.
entries.new: Petty crime is common in tourist areas, especially in the medinas and on beaches: pickpocketing, bag-snatching and drive-by motorcycle theft. People posing as official guides often harass tourists, so use only guides with an official badge. There is occasional violent crime, including knife attacks on tourists in major cities and along beaches, so avoid quiet areas after dark. Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Morocco, including in places visited by foreigners.
entries.note: The cited FCDO front page carries no safety detail; 'strong tourist-police presence', 'Marrakech and Fes' and the taxi-price advice are on no FCDO page. FCDO safety page: 'Petty crime is common in tourist areas, especially in historical districts (medina quarters) and on beaches... pickpocketing, bag-snatching, drive-by motorcycle theft'; 'It is common for people posing as official tourist guides to harass tourists'; 'Criminals have used knives against tourists in street attacks'; 'Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Morocco.' Re-cited to the safety page. EN+AR.

entries.old: Namibia is one of southern Africa's safer countries. Petty theft occurs in Windhoek, but the biggest real risks are on the road — long gravel distances, punctures, and wildlife or livestock on the road at dusk.
entries.new: Muggers often target tourists in Windhoek, and attacks can be violent, at any time of day and in busy city-centre areas. Theft from vehicles is common, particularly at service stations. Accidents are common on gravel and dirt roads: in the January–April rainy season keep below 80 km/h on gravel, carry two spare tyres and plenty of water, and avoid driving at night outside towns, where wildlife and livestock are serious hazards.
entries.note: 'One of southern Africa's safer countries' and 'petty theft' are on no FCDO page; the cited front page carries no safety detail. entries.field: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger: basis for visa-free entry
entries.old: ECOWAS citizens enter Nigeria without a visa under the bloc's free-movement protocol — up to 90 days.
entries.new: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger left ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, but the ECOWAS Commission has told member states, Nigeria included, that their citizens keep the right to move, reside and settle without a visa under ECOWAS free-movement protocols until further notice — up to 90 days per visit.
entries.note: Requirement unchanged (freedom-of-movement, 90). The old note called them ECOWAS citizens; all three left ECOWAS on 29 Jan 2025. ECOWAS Commission statement: 'the citizens of these states continue to enjoy, until further notice, the right of movement, residence and establishment without visas, in accordance with the regional organization's protocols'; the press-statement PDF says the same. Rows now cite it.

entries.old: Palau has very low crime and is one of the safest destinations in the Pacific. The real risks are in the water: strong currents, deep dives far from a recompression chamber, and boat trips through the Rock Islands in changeable weather.
entries.new: Crime levels are low — theft of unattended items is more likely than confrontational crime — but credit card fraud, including skimming, has increased. In the water, take local advice before swimming or diving from high rocks: there are over 60 vertical drop-offs, some for experienced divers only, so check a dive operator's credentials and that safety equipment, particularly oxygen, is on the boat.

entries.new: A valid visa or residence permit from Canada, the US, Australia, South Korea, Japan, the UK, Singapore or an EU country replaces the Panamanian visa (Executive Decree 521 of 2018).
entries.note: Decreto Ejecutivo 521/2018 art. 1: 'Toda persona de nacionalidad que requiere visa para ingresar a la República de Panamá, que posea Visa o Residencia vigente, debidamente expedida por Canadá, Estados Unidos de América, Mancomunidad de Australia, República de Corea, Estado del Japón, Reino Unido ..., República de Singapur y cualquiera de los Estados que conforman la Unión Europea, podrá ingresar'. No nationality is excluded, so the authorized-visa exclusion was wrong; Korea, Japan and Singapore were missing; EU, not Schengen. 61 authorized-visa and 15 stamped-visa rows rewritten, plus MO and SS.

entries.old: Travelers who would otherwise need a Panamanian visa are widely reported to be able to enter without one if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia or a Schengen country that has already been used at least once to enter the issuing country. No Panamanian government page we could read states this exemption or the length of stay it gives, and nationalities on Panama's authorized-visa list are excluded. Confirm with a Panamanian consulate or your airline before booking.
entries.new: Under Executive Decree 521 of 6 August 2018, anyone whose nationality needs a Panamanian visa may enter as a tourist without one if they hold a valid visa or residence permit issued by Canada, the United States, Australia, South Korea, Japan, the United Kingdom, Singapore or any European Union member state; the decree names the EU, not the Schengen area. The 2018 decree also required the visa to be multiple-entry, already used in the issuing country and valid for at least six more months; Executive Decree 196 of 28 October 2024 replaced that with one condition, that the visa be valid on arrival in Panama. The decrees exclude no nationality and do not state a length of stay; Panama's tourist limit is 90 days.
entries.note: The rule is now read from the decree itself (SNM-hosted Gaceta copy), not 'widely reported'. Decreto Ejecutivo 196/2024 art. 1 rewrites art. 2 of 521: 'Al momento de ingresar a territorio panameño, los ciudadanos extranjeros deberán mantener una visa vigente otorgada por uno de los países mencionados en el artículo primero'. Also confirmed by SNM's September 2026 list: 'se suprime el requisito de Visa a toda persona de nacionalidad que requiera visa ... que posea Visa o Residencia vigente'.

entries.field: FAQ: do I need a visa
entries.old: For most Western travelers, no. Citizens of the EU and EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel and most of Latin America enter visa-free for up to 90 days as tourists. Mercosur and associate-member nationals can even use a national ID card. Other nationalities need a consular visa, or a visa de arribo that a host in Paraguay files for on their behalf.

entries.old: No. Paraguay issues no electronic visa: travellers who need a visa apply at a Paraguayan embassy or consulate. The one alternative is the visa de arribo, and the traveller does not apply for it — a person or company in Paraguay does, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Dirección de Pasaportes y Servicios Consulares in Asunción, with an invitation letter, their own identity and financial documents and the traveller's completed non-resident visa form. Processing takes up to 30 days once the file is complete.

entries.old: Not checked at the border for most arrivals, but the Peruvian health ministry strongly recommends (and jungle regions expect) yellow fever vaccination for travel to the Amazon below about 2,300 m — Iquitos, Puerto Maldonado, Tarapoto and jungle lodges. entries.new: Not required for entry, but Peru's health ministry says travellers heading to jungle areas should be vaccinated at least 10 days before the trip. The endemic areas are the forested jungle of Loreto, Madre de Dios, San Martín, Ucayali and Amazonas (Iquitos, Puerto Maldonado, Tarapoto) and the jungle zones of Junín, Ayacucho, Cusco, Huánuco, Pasco and Puno — Machu Picchu and the Inca Trail are excluded.
entries.note: MINSA: endemic basins are 'zonas de selva boscosa de Loreto, Madre de Dios, San Martín, Ucayali, Amazonas y zonas de selva de Junín, Ayacucho, Cusco (excepto Machu Picchu y Camino Inca), Huánuco, Pasco y Puno'; 'Los que planean viajar a zonas de selva ... deben vacunarse al menos 10 días antes del viaje.' The ~2,300 m threshold, 'not checked at the border' and the blanket exclusion of Cusco are not stated by MINSA.

entries.old: Rwanda is one of the safest countries in Africa, with low crime and clean, orderly cities. The main caution is the border zone with the DRC (and at times Burundi), where the regional security situation can change. Check advice before visiting Rubavu or crossing to Goma.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to the parts of Rusizi District within 10 km of the border with the DRC, including the Rwandan islands in Lake Kivu and Kamembe Airport. Elsewhere crime levels are relatively low, though burglary, theft, bag-snatching and mugging occur in Kigali. Near the DRC and Burundi borders there is a risk of cross-border attacks; crossings into the DRC can close at short notice, and Burundi has kept its border with Rwanda closed since January 2024.
entries.note: FCDO (read 2026-10-03, updated 4 Sep 2026): "FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the parts of Rusizi District which are within 10km of the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), including the Rwandan islands in Lake Kivu and Kamembe Airport"; "Crime levels are relatively low in Rwanda, but there are cases of burglary, theft, bag-snatching and mugging (violent theft) in Kigali"; "Burundi closed the border to Rwanda in January 2024"; "The border crossings between Rwanda and DRC could close at short notice." The exact period is written on your stamp and is often matched to your onward ticket, so check it before leaving the airport; the Immigration Department in Castries can extend it.

entries.old: Senegal is one of West Africa's most stable democracies and most visits are trouble-free. Watch for pickpocketing and bag-snatching on Dakar's corniche and in markets, and take advice before traveling to parts of the Casamance near the Gambia and Guinea-Bissau borders, where residual caution applies off the main routes.
entries.new: Robbery, burglary and assault have become more common in Dakar, sometimes with weapons — hotels used by foreigners have been robbed at gunpoint — and pickpocketing and bag-snatching are increasing. Take care after nightfall, avoid walking alone, and pre-arrange your airport transfer, as bogus taxi drivers target arrivals. The FCDO does not advise against travel to any part of Senegal.
entries.note: FCDO Senegal 'Safety and security': 'Cases of robbery, burglary and assault have become more common in Dakar, and in some cases, involve the use of weapons. Hotels frequented by foreign nationals have been targeted and robbed at gunpoint. Street crime like pickpocketing and bag-snatching is also on the increase'; bogus airport taxis. The summary page carries no advise-against areas. The previous text's Casamance caution is not in the FCDO advice at all, and 'one of West Africa's most stable democracies' is not an FCDO statement.

entries.old: A certificate is mandatory only if you arrive from a country with yellow fever risk, but that covers most of Senegal's neighbors, and the vaccine is recommended for all visitors, so carry your yellow card.
entries.new: A certificate is required only if you arrive from a country listed as a yellow fever transmission risk — including if you only transited through an airport there — and babies aged 9 months and under are exempt. Because Senegal itself has yellow fever risk, some other countries may ask for the certificate on your onward trip.
entries.note: Repetition of the yellow-fever correction; FCDO adds 'You may need a yellow fever certificate for onward travel to some other countries, due to the risk of yellow fever in Senegal.' 'Recommended for all visitors' is not stated.

entries.old: Broadly yes — it's among West Africa's most stable countries and the tourist circuit (Dakar, Saly, Saint-Louis, Sine-Saloum) is well traveled. The main annoyances are petty theft and scams in Dakar; parts of the Casamance borderlands call for extra care.
entries.new: The FCDO does not advise against travel to any part of Senegal, but robbery, burglary and assault — sometimes armed — have become more common in Dakar, including hold-ups at hotels used by foreigners, and pickpocketing and bag-snatching are rising. Take care after dark and pre-arrange airport transfers.
entries.note: Repetition of the safety correction (Casamance caution and "most stable" not stated by FCDO; armed crime in Dakar).

entries.old: Seychelles is a safe destination with little serious crime. Petty theft from beaches, rental cars and unattended bungalows is the main issue — use hotel safes — and rip currents deserve real respect: swim where conditions are flagged safe.
entries.new: Crime is generally non-violent, but break-ins, bag snatching and thefts from parked cars, boats, guest houses, hotels and beaches occur, and people walking at night have been robbed; use a hotel safe for valuables. Beaches do not always carry safety information and some, including Beau Vallon, have dangerous rip currents when the sea is rough: ask locally before swimming and follow warning signs.
entries.note: FCDO: "Crime is generally non-violent, but people can have their bags snatched, cars and boats broken into or be robbed while walking at night"; "Beaches do not always have safety information. entries.old: Virtually every government advises against all travel to Somalia due to terrorism, armed conflict, crime and a very high kidnapping risk. Al-Shabaab regularly attacks hotels, government sites and the airport road in Mogadishu, and visitors move with pre-arranged armed security. Somaliland (Hargeisa) is calmer but remains covered by do-not-travel advisories.
entries.new: Virtually every government advises against all travel to Somalia due to terrorism, armed conflict, crime and a very high kidnapping risk. Al-Shabaab regularly attacks hotels, government sites and the airport road in Mogadishu, and visitors move with pre-arranged armed security. Somaliland is calmer: the UK advises against all but essential travel to its Awdal, Maroodijeh (Hargeisa) and Sahil regions, and against all travel to the rest of Somalia, including the rest of Somaliland.
entries.note: FCDO (updated 4 June 2026, read 2026-10-03): "FCDO advises against all travel to Somalia, including Somaliland, except for the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh, and Sahil" and "against all but essential travel to the regions of Awdal, Maroodijeh, and Sahil." Hargeisa (Maroodijeh) is under all-but-essential, not all-travel, advice from the cited source.

entries.old: Suriname is calmer than its neighbors, but street robbery happens in Paramaribo — particularly in the Palm Garden, around Waterkant after dark and in the Tourtonne area. Use taxis at night, keep valuables discreet, and treat the gold-mining districts of the interior as places to avoid.
entries.new: Burglary, armed robbery and violent crime occur in Paramaribo and the surrounding areas; criminals may target people in quiet or secluded places, including the Palm Garden (Palmentuin), and pickpocketing and robbery are increasingly common in the main business and shopping areas. Tourists have been robbed when travelling in central Suriname, away from the coast, so use a well-established tour company there.
entries.note: 'Calmer than its neighbors', Waterkant, Tourtonne and the gold-mining districts are on no FCDO page; the cited front page has no safety detail. FCDO safety page: 'burglary, armed robbery and violent crime in the capital, Paramaribo'; 'quiet or secluded areas, including in the Palm Garden (Palmentuin)'; 'Pickpocketing and robbery are increasingly common in the major business and shopping areas'; 'Tourists have been robbed when travelling in central Suriname... Use a well-established tour company'. Re-cited. EN+AR.

entries.old: Sweden is a very safe destination with low violent crime. Watch for pickpocketing in Stockholm's tourist spots and on public transport, and keep an eye on belongings in nightlife areas.
entries.new: Sweden is a safe destination for visitors. Pickpockets target tourists for passports and cash in the major cities, and gang-related crime, including shootings and explosions, has been reported in Malmö, Stockholm and Gothenburg.
entries.note: FCDO: "Take particular care of your belongings in major cities as pickpockets often target tourists for passports and cash. Violent crime does occur. Gang-related crime, including knife crime, shootings and explosions, has been reported in Malmö, Stockholm and Gothenburg." The old text's "low violent crime" contradicted this; level very-safe kept (no FCDO advisory against travel).

entries.field: How to get a Syrian visa
entries.old: Get a visa through a Syrian embassy or consulate before travel. Canada's travel advice says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain a Syrian visa at border points of entry. Rules are changing under the transitional government, so confirm with a Syrian mission shortly before traveling. (and two variants)
entries.new: Get a visa before travel. Syria's embassy in Paris says visa applications must now be made online at evisa.sy and that it no longer accepts them, but on 3 October 2026 that site showed only “Coming soon”; ask the Syrian embassy for your country how to apply. Canada's travel advice says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain a Syrian visa at border points of entry.
entries.note: 183 rows. Syrian Embassy Paris 'OBTENTION D'UN VISA': 'les demandes de visa d'entrée en Syrie devront être effectuées par voie électronique via le lien suivant https://evisa.sy — l'Ambassade de Syrie à Paris cessera de recevoir les demandes de visa'. evisa.sy/home-content (read 2026-10-03, certificate expired): 'EVisa Comming Soon'. FCDO also points to evisa.sy ('approximately 5-7 days'); Germany still says apply at the Syrian embassy in Berlin. The destination's own embassy outranks foreign advice, so 'get a visa through a Syrian embassy' no longer stands alone; requirement embassy-visa kept because the online route is not open. Unsourced 'security pre-approval' and 'rules are changing' dropped. EN+AR.

entries.old: Most travelers need a Syrian visa arranged before arrival: the UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all tell their citizens to get one in advance, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Gulf, Jordanian and Lebanese passports are shown as visa-free, but no official source we could read confirms the current rule for them; other Arab nationalities are shown as needing a visa through an embassy. Syria has announced an online eVisa, but its website was not yet taking applications in late September 2026 — confirm how to apply with a Syrian embassy shortly before travel.

entries.old: Syria remains high-risk after more than a decade of war: unexploded ordnance, sporadic fighting, terrorism and arbitrary detention are real dangers, and consular help is minimal — most governments advise against all travel. Security varies sharply by region and can change overnight.
entries.new: The UK government advises against all travel to Syria because of unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks, and it cannot provide consular support from within Syria. There is a very high threat of kidnapping by terrorist groups, and landmines and other unexploded weapons remain, especially in less populated and rural areas.
entries.note: 'Most governments advise against all travel', 'sporadic fighting', 'arbitrary detention' and 'can change overnight' are not on the FCDO pages. FCDO: 'advises against all travel to Syria due to unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks'; 'Consular support is not available from the British government from within Syria'; safety page: 'very high threat of kidnapping from terrorists throughout Syria'; 'Landmines and other unexploded weapons remain... risk in less populated and rural areas'. EN+AR.

entries.field: FAQ: how long can I stay
entries.old: Up to 90 days, but the exact period is decided by the immigration officer and shorter stamps are common if your ticket shows a short trip. You can apply to the Immigration Division for an extension of time to remain before the stamp expires.
entries.new: It depends on your passport. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU waiver agreement and South Koreans up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement; the British, Canadian, US and Japanese governments and Trinidad and Tobago’s embassy in Brazil also give 90 days, and Türkiye and Serbia 30. The Immigration Division’s no-visa list states no length of stay. In every case the immigration officer sets the period on arrival, so check your stamp, and apply to the Immigration Division for an extension of time to remain before it expires.
entries.note: 'Up to 90 days' was stated for everyone; only the EU agreement, the Korean treaty and the named governments give a figure. The no-visa list gives none.

entries.old: Yemen remains in active armed conflict and virtually all governments advise against all travel: risks include airstrikes and fighting, landmines, kidnapping and terrorism, and consular help is effectively unavailable. The island of Socotra is calmer than the mainland but is reached only on limited flights.
entries.new: The FCDO advises against all travel to the whole of Yemen because of unpredictable security conditions, and says anyone there should leave. Since July 2026 the Houthis have launched strikes on Saudi territory and shipping, with a risk of further escalation; there is a high threat of terrorism and kidnapping, and landmines are a risk on the roads. British Embassy services in Sana'a are suspended, so consular help is severely limited.
entries.note: FCDO Yemen (updated 31 Jul 2026): 'FCDO advises against all travel to the whole of the Yemen due to the unpredictable security conditions. If you're in Yemen, you should leave immediately'; 'Since July 2026, the Houthis have launched air strikes against Saudi territory and Saudi shipping'; landmines, terrorist kidnap; 'British Embassy services in Sana'a are suspended'. The FCDO says nothing about Socotra being calmer or about other governments' advice; both removed.

entries.old: Most visits — especially to Victoria Falls and the main safari circuits — are trouble-free. Petty theft occurs in cities, cash and fuel shortages flare up periodically, police roadblocks are common on intercity roads, and demonstrations should be avoided.
entries.new: Crime is moderate: mugging, pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in city centres, especially after dark, and there have been smash-and-grab robberies from cars on the airport road and some Harare routes. Physical US dollar cash is short, power cuts are frequent, and demonstrations can turn violent and should be avoided. Stop at police roadblocks and get a receipt for any fine.
entries.note: FCDO 'Safety and security': 'There is a moderate level of crime in Zimbabwe ... Mugging, pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in city centres, especially after dark'; smash-and-grab robberies on the airport route and Harare roads; 'There is a shortage of physical US dollar cash'; frequent power blackouts; demonstrations 'may turn violent'; 'stop at roadblocks ... get a receipt if you have to pay a fine'. The FCDO does not mention fuel shortages or call most visits trouble-free.
